the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm) promotes the development, conservation and sustainable management of marine ecosystems in the mediterranean and the black sea. the gfcm cooperates with croatia, bulgaria, cyprus, france, greece, italy, malta, romania, slovenia and spain, as well as with many countries in north africa and the middle east. the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean has adopted a number of recommendations to regulate the sustainable exploitation of red coral, the reduction of incidental catches of sea turtles and seals, and the high protection of endangered species of marine organisms such as sharks and rays. i supported the report on the fisheries regulations in the area of the agreement on the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean as i believe that the gfcm recommendations provide a sufficient level of safety for endangered species and sustainable fisheries.
written. i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation laying down certain provisions for fisheries in the area covered by the gfcm agreement. the technical measures adopted will help to care for protected species such as the mediterranean bear or sea turtle, as well as efforts to sustainably use economically important species such as red coral in the mediterranean, black sea and adriatic. i particularly welcome the adoption of the 14th, 18th and 19th amendments tabled by the committee on fisheries of the european parliament. the proposed text was improved by the 14th and 18th amendments from the point of view of small-scale fishermen, especially those involved in catching squid. the last of these adopted amendments is also important because of the experience of fishing in the adriatic sea. the commission has also proposed to extend the period of validity of the fishing authorisations granted to the vessels concerned by the new regulation to the period of validity of the fishing authorisations granted to the vessels concerned by the new regulation. for example, more than one third of the days spent fishing for small blue fish do not result in any net being put in the sea, for a number of reasons, such as: abrupt weather changes, the appearance of dolphins or tuna that scatter the fish, the strengthening of the sea currents, the impossibility of finding fish on certain days, and so on. the adopted amendment allows for the flexibility needed by croatian fishermen to continue with the existing fishing practice, i.e. to count only the time with registered catches in the fishing days.
written. i support the proposed package of provisions for fisheries in the area of the agreement of the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean. i believe that the package proposed, further enhanced by amendments, is a good framework for fishermen in the mediterranean. in particular, i support the provision proposed by me in the adopted amendment, which, under article 16, requires four member states to ensure that vessels equipped with trawls, seines and surrounding nets for small pelagic stocks as defined in paragraph 2 do not operate for more than 20 fishing days with a catch per month and 180 fishing days with a catch per year. i consider that this provision is fairer to the fishermen and that the days when no catches were made should not be deducted from the days permitted to fishermen for their activities. this is especially true of croatian swimming fishermen, who can only fish on days without a moon and who, unlike floating carts, are also threatened by predators and currents. this provision will also allow more accurate statistics to be kept on days without catches, fishing effort, etc., which can be used to develop future technical management measures.

development cooperation into the spotlight throughout the whole year. the eu has been engaged in development cooperation since 1957. it has long been the largest donor of official development assistance in the world and aspires to continue to remain the largest donor for the years to come. this is something we can be proud of, but it is also something which is unknown to many of our own citizens, however supportive they are of development cooperation. hence we need to communicate more and better on what we do. the european year for development will highlight the results that the eu, acting together with its member states, has achieved and will continue to strive for in the future. we will work to foster direct involvement and critical thinking on the part of eu citizens and stakeholders in development cooperation. we want to show that eu development cooperation is good not only for eu partner countries but also for eu citizens. in a changing and increasingly interdependent world in which major shifts have taken place in the global economic and political balance, we should spare no effort to stimulate a sense of shared responsibility and solidarity among citizens in europe and in partner countries. the 2014 eurobarometer paints a clear picture. more than 85% of eu citizens say that the eu should continue development cooperation efforts, and 67% think that the eu should actually be giving more aid. this is despite the current economic difficulties. at the same time, eu citizens also demand that we use public funds effectively and efficiently to achieve concrete results in terms of reducing poverty and building a more stable, peaceful, prosperous and equitable world. in 2015, the international community will have to agree on a new post-2015 development agenda. we will have the third financing for development conference in july in addis ababa, the un post-2015 summit in september, and the global climate agreement at cop 21 in paris in the most important topics related to development: education, gender, food security, demography, immigration, human rights and governance, to name but a few. the eu institutions and member states, but jean-claude juncker, ms federica mogherini, the prime minister of latvia, ms laimdota straujuma and the chair of the committee on development of the european parliament, ms linda mcavan. the riga austria, ireland and france are some examples. the member states will organise a large number of events and activities at all levels throughout the year. in addition to the riga event last week, in march the latvian presidency will hold a high-level conference in riga on gender, women’s economic empowerment and sustainable development in the post-2015 agenda. apart from high-visibility events in latvia, we have centralised the activities to make the year as close to the citizens as possible. it will be implemented by all relevant stakeholders, ngos, private sector representatives, academia, line ministries and local authorities. in may, expo milan will open its doors to thousands of visitors, involving them and inviting them to reflect on the theme of ‘feeding the planet, energy for life’. this will be another unique opportunity for the eu to showcase the achievements of its development policy. i would like to underline how well the european parliament, the council, the member enthusiastic rapporteur. the discussions and exchanges between the european parliament and the council have always been constructive. the programme of activities prepared by the european parliament will make a significant contribution to that success. i have no doubt that we will all continue to demonstrate the shared sense of commitment and implementation throughout 2015. i can assure you that the presidency will do its utmost to ensure the success of this important endeavour.

vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs. – madam president, let me thank you for this exchange of views today regarding the situation in the democratic republic of congo. as you know, the european union has been a strong and consistent partner to the democratic republic of congo (drc) over the last 15 years. in 2006 it provided the bulk of financing for the organisation of the first democratic elections in the history of congo and the drc has been one of our top priorities in africa over the past decades. this includes two military operations and a sustained effort to support security sector reform with two csdp missions, as well as more traditional areas of cooperation such as health, roads and natural resources management. today i think that many of you are especially concerned about the delays and uncertainties surrounding the electoral process, which includes the holding of local elections in 2015 and the legislative and presidential elections in 2016 at the latest. the recent debate over the passing of a new electoral law has led to violent popular protests calling for constitutional timelines to be respected, and to two casualties. during this difficult time we called on all political forces to seek a consensus to facilitate an appeasement of the situation, and we asked the government in particular to exercise constraint, to maintain an open political space and allow for the peaceful expression of opinion. the prerequisite of organising a general consensus before the legislative and presidential elections has now been dropped. this opens the door to organising the elections within the constitutional timeframe. this is a very positive step which i welcome and i know too that some of you expressed opinions on the same lines. but respect for the constitution goes further than respecting timelines. freedoms of speech and of the media, the right of peaceful assembly, respect for the rights of the opposition are all essential components of a democracy. these critical elements will be part of our dialogue with the congolese government, with the objective of reducing tensions in the political climate. i am very much aware of, and i share, the concerns of this parliament regarding the situation of dr denis mukwege and the panzi hospital. let me say too that i was honoured, personally, to sit in this very same room, listening to his inspiring and dramatic words last november on the occasion of the sakharov prize. i was also honoured to have on that occasion a very good meeting with him, looking for ways of cooperating on concrete projects. i wish to confirm to you that the european union is following with great vigilance the situation concerning his physical security as a human rights defender. i have also asked my representative in kinshasa to enquire about the dispute between the congolese administration and the panzi hospital. i strongly support an amicable agreement between the panzi hospital and the congolese administration. the holding of democratic elections leading to a peaceful transition of power will be key to longer-term stability in the drc and in the wider region. stability will also depend on other factors, in particular the neutralisation of all armed groups in eastern congo. there has been some significant progress in this respect thanks to the efforts of the congolese army and monusco. nevertheless, important challenges remain: for example regarding the ex-m23 movement. the governments of the drc, uganda and rwanda should strengthen their collaboration to achieve a durable disarmament, demobilisation and reintegration of ex-combatants and their dependents. the fdlr rebel group remains a major threat to long-term stability in the region. linked with the rwanda 1994 genocide ideology, this group has inflicted immense human suffering and has spoiled drc–rwanda relations. with the support of the united nations, there is now a unique opportunity to address one of the root causes of conflicts in the kivus. the fdlr movement has been given plenty of time by countries in the region to surrender peacefully. we discussed this in the foreign affairs council in january and we adopted 28 council conclusions where we stated that the time has now come for military operations. however we stress too that we invite monusco and fardc to ensure civilians are fully protected and that international humanitarian law is respected during the operations. let me reiterate our support for the un involvement in promoting peace and stability. this includes the sustained efforts of monusco and troop-contributing countries as well as the personal efforts of the un special envoy for the great lakes region. let me also stress that i know, and i share, your desire to curb the links between conflict and exploitation of natural resources in the great lakes region. as part of its comprehensive approach the european union has started to address the situation. together with the commission, as you might very well know, my predecessor issued a joint communication on responsible sourcing of conflict minerals. and parliament and the council are currently examining right now the draft regulations that went together with this communication. finally, i would like to mention the european union’s long-term commitment in the drc to supporting the preservation of congolese national parks. this includes virunga park, which is part of the unesco world heritage sites. the future of this park is threatened by permits being granted for oil exploration that could lead to oil exploitation in the future. let me ensure you that we will continue to keep a close eye on national decisions that might impact on the sustainability of this park. to conclude, i would just like to share with you the information that i have mandated mr vervaeke, the eu senior coordinator for the great lakes region, to join a mission of special envoys that will go to kinshasa in the coming weeks to assess the situation and obviously report back. i thank you for your attention and i look forward to the debate and listening to your speeches today.

written. i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a council decision on the declaration by which the member states accept, in the interest of the european union, gabon's accession to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction, as the protection and promotion of the rights of children is one of the priorities of the union. this includes preventive measures to prevent child abduction and international cooperation. i believe that coordinated measures are needed to return abducted children to their country of residence. i therefore believe that such cases should be governed by the applicable law of the country in which the children are resident and that there is a need to condemn and warn against such acts.
the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction is an important instrument that has been ratified by all eu member states. the convention establishes a system of cooperation between states aimed at resolving cases of international child abduction. it is common for a child's parents to live apart in different countries, so the biggest problem is the national bias of the legal systems of individual countries. it is possible that the courts in both countries will declare that they have jurisdiction and that custody of the child will be granted to each of the parents who are their nationals. the convention is intended to address such situations at the international level by establishing that the courts and applicable laws are only those of the state of the child's residence. the convention also implements a system that ensures the automatic return of children who have been abducted. the european union now has exclusive competence in this area, as confirmed by the european court of justice. i support the council decision inviting the member states to accept gabon's accession to the convention as this is in the interest of the european union, it will contribute to the coherence and uniformity of the application of union law.
written. international child abduction is synonymous with international parental kidnapping, however legally, international child abduction originates from private international law and refers to the illegal removal of children from their home by an acquaintance or family member to a foreign country. in this context, "illegality" derives from "violation of custody rights", and "home" is defined as the child's habitual residence. as implied, "custody violation" is a phenomenon of international child abduction that typically involves illegal alienation, creating a conflict of jurisdiction of law, multiple authorities and jurisdictions. they can reach seemingly reasonable but also conflicting custody decisions with geographically limited application. such an outcome often negatively affects the child's access to and relationship with the opposite sex of the family and may cause the loss of their former language, culture, name and nationality, which violates numerous children's rights and may cause serious psychological and emotional trauma to the child and the family. the harmful consequences of such behaviour for children and families have been demonstrated in several studies, and international child abduction has been identified as a form of parental alienation and child abuse. the accession of gabon to the 1980 hague convention provides for the protection of children in the event of adverse developments in the personal relationships of their parents.

written. every year, eight million children disappear worldwide, which would mean that nearly 22,000 children disappear every day. all our efforts should be directed towards securing a better future for our children, and so this convention, signed by all the member states of the european union, should ensure a secure future and the realisation of all children's rights. as the report states, the most common problems are the agreement of the court's jurisdiction over the custody of children whose parents are from different countries, as well as the lack of communication between the two countries. the convention is designed to have such cases handled by predetermined courts of competent jurisdiction and to have the prescribed laws applied. the countries that join the convention enter into a common system for dealing with child abduction. if the legal systems differ too much and the country does not have the means to establish a body to enforce the laws and proposals of this convention, the country cannot even access it. that is precisely the problem with gabon's accession to the hague convention. gabon acceded to the convention on 6 december 2010 and it entered into force on 1 march 2011. in order to address the abduction of children in gabon and the european union, i support this report for the acceptance of the accession to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction.
written. i support gabon's accession to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction, as this ensures timely and comprehensive protection for vulnerable children. the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction is an important instrument that has been ratified by 86 countries to date, including all members of the european union. abduction problems often arise when parents divorce, especially if the mother and father are from different countries. the purpose of the convention is to resolve these cases at the international level, by establishing competent courts and appropriate laws. proposals for third countries to accede to the convention have no impact on the budget of the european union and the prevention of child abduction forms an essential part of the eu's policy to promote children's rights. the european union is therefore actively encouraging third countries to accede to the convention, and i support the report.
written. - preventing child abduction is an important part of the european union's policy to promote children's rights. the eu's international action is therefore also very important in order to improve the application of the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction. the convention thus establishes a system of cooperation between states parties to the convention aimed at resolving cases of international child abduction in the event of divorce of parents from different states. the problem arises in the part where the convention does not provide for the autonomous action of international organisations and therefore a council decision is required calling on the member states to accept, each in relation to its territory, the accession of gabon to the convention and thus the effective entry into force of the convention in cases involving the eu and that country. it is desirable that the acceptance report on gabon's accession takes effect after the establishment of the central authority assisting eu citizens in this case. i think that gabon's accession to the convention is very welcome, because many eu citizens are of gabonese origin, and in this way children associated with the gabonese community will be protected from abduction. it is therefore proposed that this proposal be adopted by parliament without amendments, in order to ensure the comprehensive protection of the european union as regards children.
written. this document concerns cooperation between states in the case of international child abduction. in fact, when parents come from different countries, it is not uncommon for them to take advantage of loopholes and the lack of clearly defined cooperation between countries in the event of a break-up or divorce to illegally adopt a child. the hague convention therefore seeks to establish clear international practices in such cases. the best interests of the child come first, and that's why i support the report.
written. i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a council decision on the declaration by which the member states accept, in the interest of the european union, the accession of andorra to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction, because i believe that the protection of children should be a priority at global level. only this kind of action can fundamentally and concretely address this problem of global scale, which has different causes and connotations. i support the accession of andorra to this convention because i am confident that within the legal framework that the convention provides for andorra, it will further strengthen activities aimed at combating the problem of child abduction.
the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction is an important instrument that has been ratified by all eu member states. the convention establishes a system of cooperation between states aimed at resolving cases of international child abduction. it is common for a child's parents to live apart in different countries, so the biggest problem is the national bias of the legal systems of individual countries. it is possible that the courts in both countries will declare that they have jurisdiction and that custody of the child will be granted to each of the parents who are their nationals. the convention is intended to address such situations at the international level by establishing that the courts and applicable laws are only those of the state of the child's residence. the convention also implements a system that ensures the automatic return of children who have been abducted. the european union now has exclusive competence in this area, as confirmed by the european court of justice. i support the council decision inviting the member states to accept andorra's accession to the convention as this is in the interest of the european union, it will contribute to the coherence and uniformity of the application of union law.

the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction is an important instrument that has been ratified by all eu member states. the convention establishes a system of cooperation between states aimed at resolving cases of international child abduction. it is common for a child's parents to live apart in different countries, so the biggest problem is the national bias of the legal systems of individual countries. it is possible that the courts in both countries will declare that they have jurisdiction and that custody of the child will be granted to each of the parents who are their nationals. the convention is intended to address such situations at the international level by establishing that the courts and applicable laws are only those of the state of the child's residence. the convention also implements a system that ensures the automatic return of children who have been abducted. the european union now has exclusive competence in this area, as confirmed by the european court of justice. i support the council decision inviting the member states to accept the accession of morocco to the convention, as this is in the interest of the european union, it will contribute to the coherence and uniformity of the application of union law.

written. ‒ the aim of changing the maximum authorised weight in road transport is to reduce energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions, to adapt legislation to technological developments and to adapt to market needs and facilitate intermodal transport. the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions as well as the reduction of the consumption of petroleum products in the transport sector has become crucial, even crucial for road transport, which accounts for 82% of the energy consumption in the transport sector. in addition, the increase in fuel prices is driving the need to identify solutions to reduce vehicle fuel consumption and consequently reduce greenhouse gas emissions. the white paper on transport set a target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 60% by 2050 compared to 1990 levels. in this context, it announced a revision of the 1996 directive with a view to introducing more energy-efficient vehicles on the eu market. energy efficiency must be one of the priorities of the european union, which is why i support the report by mr leichtfriede and the objectives it sets.
written. ‒ in order to protect the environment, increase energy efficiency and reduce fossil fuel consumption, the council has accepted waste heat as one of the main sources of alternative fuels. the use of alternative sources reduces environmental pollution but has an impact on the increase in the total mass of the vehicle. in the case of intermodal transport of containers of 45 feet in length, trailers and semi-trailers 15 cm longer than the length of the container are placed on the market and the transport of which required special permits. in order to maximise energy efficiency, motor vehicles shall be equipped with aerodynamic retractors or retractable aerodynamic devices attached to the rear of the vehicle. the new cab design should have increased aerodynamic performance, which, in addition to the energy factor, greatly improves the overall road safety of the vehicle and the driver's comfort. the commission should be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 290 tfeu concerning the definition of the criteria for the recognition of the right to the protection of personal data. i therefore support the report by mr leichtfriede and the directive and believe that technical adaptations should be introduced, fuel consumption and co2 emissions reduced, road infrastructure protected and free competition ensured.
written. ‒ i supported the report on the dimensions and masses of road vehicles in circulation within the community because i believe it is essential to emphasise the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, in particular carbon dioxide (co2) emissions, and to improve road safety by adapting the relevant legislation to technological developments and changing market needs. the above affects the strengthening of the sustainable growth of the community as a whole. although at first glance the dimensions and masses of road vehicles are not directly related to the above, the fact is that a better vehicle design will result in less air resistance and thus less fuel consumption, which ultimately means less greenhouse gas emissions and less pollution. considering that the transition to alternative propulsion systems involves a system that draws energy from batteries or other electrical energy storage devices for the purposes of mechanical propulsion, we will also see how their use in heavy goods vehicles or buses also increases the mass of the vehicle. in addition to environmental efficiency, i believe that the implementation of the directive would also contribute to road safety, as new designs, such as rounded cabs, would increase the driver's visibility and make it easier to spot other road users. in view of the aforementioned effective possibilities, i call on the member states to cooperate effectively at international level in which the european institutions will be informed of the checks carried out by their competent authorities in road transport.
written. ‒ i support this resolution which aims to allow the installation of retractable or folding aerodynamic devices at the rear of the vehicle, thereby enabling significant improvements in the energy performance of the vehicle. the fitting of a vehicle with a new cab design would contribute to improving road safety by reducing blind spots in the driver's field of vision, including those under the windscreen, and should help save the lives of many vulnerable road users such as pedestrians or cyclists. the road components of intermodal transport activities can currently only be carried out if both member states and carriers implement complex administrative procedures or if these containers have patented embossed edges, which creates extremely high costs. the increase of the authorised length of vehicles carrying such containers by 15 cm could relieve carriers of those administrative procedures and facilitate intermodal transport activities without endangering or harming the road infrastructure or other road users.
written. i support this report because it defines weight limits for alternative fuel vehicles. the council accepted waste heat as a type of alternative fuel and added weight for three-axle buses using alternative fuels. the transport procedure for transporting one or more containers or interchangeable boxes up to a total maximum length of 45 feet is also defined. the manufacture of longer cabs is allowed if they are more energy efficient and safer. the commission will reassess the directive 3 years after its implementation in national legislation.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending directive 96/53/ec on the determination of the dimensions and weights of certain road vehicles circulating within the community. adapting legislation to changing market needs as well as technological developments is necessary to regulate the road transport sector effectively and to guarantee its safety. the proposal emphasises the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and in particular carbon dioxide emissions, in order to contribute to the objectives of the white paper on transport and to ensure energy efficiency. the proposal also highlights provisions aimed at improving working conditions and the protection of road users, all with the aim of improving safety. i think that member states should retain the right to create transport solutions that are appropriate to the conditions on their territory. i also support the provisions that highlight the need for efficient and high-quality inspection supervision in order to improve energy efficiency and aerodynamics of vehicles, and to improve road safety.

written. ‒ in retail, the average consumer is unaware that credit card charges are included in the price of the product. the fee cap will affect 95% of all card payments and mean savings to customers of just over €730 million per year. the commission also notes that the commission has not provided any information on the level of the credit risk of the credit card. this is very good news for consumers in croatia, especially when you consider that there are twice as many credit cards in croatia as there are people. unlike germans who pay a card transaction fee of 1.8 percent, or danes who pay 0.1 percent, in croatia the card transaction costs reach up to 5 percent. the end result will be greater consumer protection, lower prices for goods and services, and big savings for both consumers and traders.

president-in-office of the council.– madam president, to date the ebola virus disease has taken a heavy toll on life: almost 24 000 people have been infected and more than 9 800 have died. it is a global problem. no country in the world can feel completely safe as the ebola virus disease does not respect national borders, and is a challenge that demands our highest attention. the presidency welcomes the high-level conference on ebola from emergency to recovery organised by, and under the patronage of, the european union, in close cooperation with the united nations and the governments of the three most affected countries – liberia, sierra leone and guinea. the presidency would like to convey its gratitude to high representative federica mogherini and to the eu ebola coordinator, commissioner stylianides, and also to commissioner mimica and commissioner andriukaitis for an outstanding organisation of this event. the large number of high-level speakers and participants representing the affected region, the eu and its member states, international organisations, un agencies and ngos, proved that the international community is greatly concerned by, and actively engaged against, the ebola virus disease. we are cooperating in a joint effort to combat this dreadful epidemic. commissioner stylianides will, i believe, go into much greater detail in the work and the outcomes of the conference, but let me, for my part, share some thoughts from the council’s point of view. this conference confirms that despite the stabilisation of the outbreak, the international community must ‘keep up the momentum’ and continue to provide the international aid, which is essential. we cannot afford to become complacent. we have to maintain our attention on the response to the epidemic and prevent any increase in infections. our efforts need to focus on the target of bringing the number of infections to zero because even a single case not identified quickly enough can pose a significant threat. the target of bringing the number of infections to zero, and maintaining that level, is ambitious, yet, by working together, we can achieve it. the conference took place at a crucial moment as we are moving from the emergency response to the recovery phase. it marked a step forward, for participants to look ahead, discuss the lessons learned and start focusing on recovery and reconstruction of public services, enhancement of preparedness, alert and response systems, health, education, risk communication, social protection and reviving the economies of the affected countries and of other countries with a potential risk of outbreak of the disease. all the participants shared the opinion that the crisis can only be solved with a common and comprehensive approach addressing critical gaps in essential services, allowing the affected countries and countries which are at potential risk to build long—term resilience and protect themselves from future shocks. the ebola virus disease is primarily a regional problem. therefore, the presidency welcomes the commitment of the presidents of the three affected countries – guinea, liberia and sierra leone – to establish coordinated regional recovery plans together with roadmaps and coordinating structures. this conference has shown once again the commitment of the eu and its member states in tackling the epidemic and assisting the countries in need. the eu reacted quickly. several mechanisms were rapidly activated such as the eu civil protection mechanism and the health security committee. starting from early september, the council and the european council provided political guidance for the eu response and worked on the basis of the ambitious objective of mobilising financial aid amounting to eur 1 billion. we have surpassed that objective, and have provided also in—kind assistance and expertise, thus giving the eu one of the leading roles in the global ebola response. last october, the european council nominated commissioner stylianides as the eu ebola coordinator. today and tomorrow, we must work along the lines identified by the conference, notably, to ensure that funds already pledged are made available and maintain international support until there are no more ebola cases. we must also make the response more mobile and flexible; promote regional cooperation; assist countries in west africa on prevention, containment and preparedness and help them build resilient health systems; and we must also improve governance and accountability of local and national systems. international engagement needs to be maintained, and i note that further high—level meetings will be held in washington next month. the council also welcomes the valuable support of the european parliament in addressing the ebola crisis. discussions in different committees, debate in the plenary and the resolution adopted in september by the european parliament gave an important signal to the international community on the eu’s dedication to overcome the epidemic. the council is looking forward to the report by charles goerens that will serve as an important element in further discussions on the lessons learned and on the strengthening of health systems in developing countries to prevent future crises. allow me to conclude by expressing our deepest tribute and appreciation to the constant dedication of health workers and international governmental and non-governmental organisations to tackle the ebola epidemics, their exceptional courage, self-sacrifice and professionalism. i would like to thank you very much right now for having this debate tonight and i also look forward to a fruitful discussion.
member of the commission.– mr president, it is very important that we are having this discussion today, only one week after the high—level conference on ebola, as has already been said by the presidency. it proves once again the interest of parliament in our fight against the virus, against its tangible consequences on the ground. allow me to share with you a brief assessment of the conference we organised last week in brussels. first, the conference succeeded in bringing together all the key actors in the fight against ebola. in a joint effort between the european union and the three affected countries, their presidents played a central role in the proceedings, but also involving the united nations and the west african region, as well as the african union. why do i insist on this joint effort? because everything we do in the fight against ebola needs to be done with, and for, the affected countries, especially their people. second, the conference underlined the fact that our immediate priority still has to be to ‘get to zero cases’ in all three countries and sustain this for 42 days. you know very well the medical conditions and that we need to further adjust our response in the field. of course, by shifting from big treatment centres to community—level response, out in the provinces, we have to work even more with communities. this was timely because, while liberia may now be close to a sustainable ‘zero’, case numbers have unfortunately again been going up in sierra leone and guinea. third, the conference reflected the joined—up way in which we as the european union have approached ebola – as a collective effort between federica mogherini, neven mimica, vytenis andriukaitis, carlos moedas and myself as ebola coordinator, with the commission and the eeas working together to get things done, as we have been doing ever since the ebola outbreak started. the conference also heard how an unprecedented research effort is helping in the fight to get to zero, and how the european union, through fast—tracking very substantial amounts of research funding, is making a big contribution to meeting the research priorities identified by the who. the achieve this. fourth, the conference agreed a framework for recovery of the three countries. it heard how massively ebola has hit their economies, which were on a path of strong growth before ebola. the co—chairs’ conclusions from the conference set out the key sectors on which the recovery effort needs to focus: healthcare, certainly, to provide people with basic care, and to make sure the three countries are better prepared to deal with future epidemics; but also water and sanitation, nutrition, and social safety nets, with, of course, a particular focus on the most vulnerable. in the very short term, there is a need to vaccinate people, and provide primary care, clean water, and sanitation. if we do not invest in these things, it will be just a matter of time before another epidemic erupts. so we now have a common roadmap with strong support from the three presidents. the next steps will be a discussion on the fringes of the world bank spring meetings, in april, and then a un—led pledging conference at the end of may. fifth, and very important, the conference provided a big boost for regional cooperation. this became one of my top objectives upon my arrival from the ebola—affected countries last november. over the last few months, the three countries have taken concrete steps in that direction. the presence of the three leaders in brussels last week and their mutual commitment are very encouraging, and all actors agree that this is crucial for preventing and containing future epidemics. as the european union, we are already providing hands—on support for cross—border preparedness in the region. we will look at how to strengthen this further. in short, the conference more than lived up to expectations; but it is part of a process – not the end point, but the beginning. finally, a word of thanks to the european parliament delegation to the conference: linda mcavan, louis michel, charles goerens and michelle rivasi. the european parliament’s contribution to the discussion was greatly appreciated.

written. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a regulation of the parliament and of the council on common rules for imports from certain third countries, as this does not affect the substance of the proposal but is mainly a matter of technical amendments. in a very important area such as trade policy, it is crucial that eu law is made clearer and more accessible to citizens. i consider that the codification and amendment of this regulation will contribute to legal certainty and reduce the need for research activities when searching for the rules in force.
written. ‒ this proposal amends and codifies regulation (ec) no 625/2009 of the european parliament and of the council on common rules for imports from certain third countries. the basic act regulates the introduction of safeguard and surveillance instruments applicable to imports of products, including imports of coal and steel from a limited number of countries such as azerbaijan, kazakhstan, belarus, turkmenistan, uzbekistan and north korea. this proposed change updates the appendix to the regulation and removes from the list the countries that have meanwhile become members of the world trade organisation: armenia, russia, tajikistan and vietnam. the act will not undergo any other substantive changes. since i expect that the amended text will contribute to greater legal certainty in the application of the act in relations, both between eu countries and those third countries and between their economic operators in trade covered by the provisions of the regulation, i supported this proposal.
written. ‒ the consultative working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission is of the opinion that the commission proposal does not contain any substantive changes other than those indicated as such in the proposal and that the proposal, as regards the codification of the unchanged provisions of the previous acts and those amendments, is limited to the codification of existing acts without substantial changes to them, and i therefore support it.
written. ‒ i support the welsh mp's report because it is important to codify this technical proposal for a regulation which talks about common rules for imports in general, but also for imports of textiles from certain third countries. following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, a new act was needed to ensure that the previous decisions were aligned with the new acts. this was achieved by the omnibus i and ii acts, which amend a number of trade-related regulations, including the regulation on common rules for imports from certain third countries. the most important changes were made in terms of the removal from the list of 'third countries' that have become members of the world trade organisation. the common commercial policy should be based on uniform principles, taking into account the specific characteristics of the economic systems in third countries. the liberalisation of imports, namely the absence of quantitative restrictions, should therefore be the starting point for union rules, and in the case of protection of the union's interests, the commission is competent to adopt safeguard measures, taking into account international obligations.
written. ‒ the commission proposal concerns the codification and recasting of regulation (ec) no 625/2009 on common rules for imports from certain third countries. the commission has also proposed to extend the scope of the proposal to include the protection and surveillance instruments applicable to imports of products including coal and steel, but excluding textiles subject to a specific regulation. the regulation concerns only a limited number of countries, namely azerbaijan, belarus, kazakhstan, north korea, turkmenistan and uzbekistan. the safeguard instrument is rarely used in practice and as far as surveillance is concerned, the last surveillance measure in force for steel products expired on 31 december 2012. the main change concerns the update of the additions for removal for the countries that have now become members of the world trade organisation, namely armenia, russia, tajikistan and vietnam. i would like to emphasise that the advisory working group has unanimously decided that the proposal does not contain any significant changes other than those already identified, and therefore i support the report.

written. the purpose of this report is to codify the above-mentioned council and parliament regulation without any substantive changes. the presidency of the european council in edinburgh in 1992 confirmed the codification of all procedures after more than ten amendments, stressing their importance. the new proposal for a regulation fully preserves the unique content of the acts. the main codified provisions contain a proposal laying down certain procedures for the adoption of detailed rules for the implementation of the provisions of the stabilisation and association agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of montenegro, of the other part. it provides that fishery products originating in montenegro may be imported into the european union at a reduced customs duty, within the limits of tariff quotas. it is therefore necessary to lay down provisions governing the management of those tariff quotas. the proposal lays down in particular concessions for fish, fishery products and certain tariff reductions and lays down conditions concerning safeguard clauses for agricultural and fishery products. in my view, these measures should be adopted in accordance with a regulation of the european parliament and of the council and the commission should adopt immediately applicable acts.

written. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council opening and providing for the administration of certain union tariff quotas for high-quality beef, pigmeat, poultrymeat, wheat and sorghum and soya beans and other residues, as i believe that the european union's law in this area must be as clear and transparent as possible. the european union must make its legal acts easier and more effective to find and understand, and codification is moving in that direction. this proposal guarantees legal certainty and reduces the need for research work in order to find out what rules are in force.
‒ the european commission decided on 1 april 1987 that no more than 10 amendments to an act should be codified, citing the recommendation of the european council confirmed in edinburgh in december 1992, and on 20 december 1994 an agreement was reached between the european parliament, the council and the commission which further accelerated the process of codification by adopting the appropriate legal instruments. council regulation (ec) no 774/94 of 29 march 1994 opening and providing for the application of certain union tariff quotas for high-quality beef, pigmeat, poultrymeat, wheat and meslin, and for soya beans and other residues has been amended several times. the regulation governs the terms reached in the course of the negotiations on tariff concessions under article xxviii of the general agreement on tariffs and trade (gatt) and agreed during the uruguay round of multilateral trade negotiations on quotas. the basic regulation aimed at opening annual union tariff quotas for high-quality products. the proposal for a new regulation will bring together the different actions covered by the previous amendments and fully preserve the substance of the act. in order to ensure that the proposed codification is applied correctly among the shares to which it has legal effect, i consider it necessary as it contributes to greater legal certainty in the application of the act and have therefore supported this proposal.
written. ‒ according to the advisory group of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission, the proposal in question is limited to the codification of existing texts without any substantive changes. this formal procedure increases the transparency of the process and allows citizens to be fully informed about this issue through simplified rules, which is why i support it.

written. the basic text of council regulation (ec) no 1506/98 of 29 march 1994 suspending certain concessions relating to the importation into the union of agricultural products originating in turkey provides for the suspension of certain concessions in respect of imbalances in trade between member states in agricultural products resulting from the application of certain prohibitions on imports of certain agricultural products into turkey from the eu. in particular, turkey has applied a ban on the import of live animals (beef) since 1996 and has imposed restrictions on imports of beef from the european union. in order to protect the union's trade interests, the provisions of the regulation have taken appropriate reciprocal measures and some of the existing concessions have been suspended. the regulation has been amended several times and needs to be codified. on 1 april 1987, the european commission decided that no more than ten amendments to an act should be codified, citing the recommendation of the european council confirmed in edinburgh in december 1992, and on 20 december 1994 an agreement was reached between the european parliament, the council and the commission which further accelerated the process of codification by adopting the appropriate legal instruments. the proposal for a new regulation will harmonise the acts and procedures covered by the previous amendments and fully preserve the substance of the act. in order to ensure the correct application of this regulation, i consider the proposed codification to be justified.

written. ‒ the agreement establishing the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm), in accordance with the provisions of article xiv of the fao constitution, was approved at the 1949 session of the fao conference and entered into force in 1952. the gfcm is a regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo) whose objective is to promote the development, conservation and optimum exploitation of living marine resources and their rational management as well as the sustainable development of aquaculture in the mediterranean and black sea. these amendments to the agreement revised the structure and content of the existing agreement to bring it into line with the latest rfmo instruments. the amended agreement is consistent with the main objectives of the common fisheries policy. the aim of the proposal is to conclude the amended gfcm agreement on behalf of the european union, which i support.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the draft council decision adopting the amended agreement establishing the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean, as it gives its consent to the conclusion of an agreement that will modernise and upgrade the commission in question and strengthen its role in the conservation of marine resources. i believe that it is essential to ensure the sustainable and coordinated exploitation of marine resources and ecosystems in order to achieve their long-term and balanced conservation. in this context, it is important to clearly articulate the overarching objective of the biosocial, economic and environmental sustainability of living marine resources and to better define the responsibilities of the general commission and the relevant sanctions. the commission shall be assisted by the european parliament and the council.
written. ‒ this amendment to the agreement sets a clear general objective of the biological, social, economic and environmental sustainability of living marine resources and provides new definitions of terms necessary for a correct interpretation of the agreement establishing the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean. the gfcm's role should be further defined to include the promotion of joint fisheries management through multiannual management plans, the establishment of restricted fishing areas and the collection and exchange of data. in this sense, the new agreement covers the basic components of the common fisheries policy relating to: maximising sustainable yield, protecting ecosystems and applying the precautionary principle, reducing discards and combating illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. in addition, the amendment to the agreement establishes provisions to determine measures and sanctions to address non-coordinated conduct by non-gfcm parties and establishes a well-defined mechanism for resolving disputes if they arise between the parties to the agreement. as croatia is a party to the agreement, i believe that a clearer regulation of these areas will contribute to a better implementation of a fisheries policy aimed at greater yield sustainability and ecosystem protection, and at the same time allow better communication of the exceptions and needs of specific mediterranean areas such as the croatian islands or the islands in the aegean sea.
‒ the gfcm is a regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo) whose objective is to promote the development, conservation and optimum exploitation of living marine resources and their rational management as well as the sustainable development of aquaculture in the mediterranean and the black sea. the amendment of the gfcm agreement was launched in 2013 following a performance review finalised in 2011 which concluded that the agreement needed to be amended in order to clarify the objectives and functions of the gfcm and to increase its effectiveness. in this context, the new agreement covers the basic components of the common fisheries policy relating to the objective of maximum sustainable yield, ecosystems and precautionary approach, reducing discards and combating illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. i support the amended agreement which is in line with the main objectives of the common fisheries policy. the proposal aims to conclude the amended gfcm agreement on behalf of the european union and i hope that, in addition to meeting the basic objectives of the common fisheries policy, the traditional and cultural specificities of our fishermen will also be taken into account. this is primarily for small-scale fishermen who are completely marginalised by the existing system, even though it is a tradition and a way of life, not a disruption of the ecosystem and a profitable activity.
written. ‒ i support the agreement to establish a general commission for mediterranean fisheries, primarily because i represent croatia, a mediterranean and adriatic country which by its very position has an interest in investing in long-term development, the use of living marine resources, the preservation of ecosystems and the healthy coexistence of man and nature. i believe that this amendment creates a more convincing and better picture of the agreement itself because it sets clear objectives in terms of biological, social, economic policy of the sea and sustainable development. the commission's own role in fisheries, which includes promoting joint fisheries management through multiannual plans and the establishment of fisheries protection areas, is better defined. the agreement covers the basic elements of normal fishing procedures relating to maximum sustainable yield, the fight against all types of poaching and the reduction of fish arrivals. the regulation lays down penalties in the event of non-compliance by member states. the parties shall cooperate in the implementation of this agreement. the aim of this agreement is primarily to protect the 'blue ribbon', which is a long-term strategy and to support the sustainable development of the marine and coastal sector as a whole. they must be the drivers of europe's economy and have a great potential for innovation and growth. so i reiterate that we all need to insist on smart and sustainable growth and development in accordance with nature and human needs.
written. ‒ the amendments to the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm) agreement were launched in 2013 and after a performance review finalised in 2011, it was concluded that the agreement should be amended to clarify the objectives and functions of the gfcm and to enhance its effectiveness. the negotiations were conducted between the member states and the commission and within their respective areas of competence in accordance with the terms of the mandate. the amended agreement revises the structure and content of the current one in order to bring it into line with the modern rfmo instruments. the aim of the new agreement is to set a clear overall objective of biological, social, economic and environmental sustainability of natural resources. it also provides definitions of terms necessary for the proper interpretation of the agreement. the more defined functions of the gfcm include the promotion of joint fisheries management through multiannual management plans, the establishment of fisheries in restricted areas, and the collection and dissemination of data. in this context, the new agreement integrates the fundamental objectives of maximum sustainable yield, ecosystems, reducing discharges, combating illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, and i therefore support it.
written. the commission, on behalf of the european union, invites the council to adopt a decision approving the amended treaty establishing the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean, known as the regional fisheries management organisation, with the aim of promoting the development, conservation, rational management and best use of living marine resources and the sustainable development of aquaculture in the mediterranean and the black sea. the amendments to the general commission agreement were launched in 2013 to clarify its objectives and functions and to enhance its effectiveness. the revised agreement revises the structure and content of the existing agreement and sets clear targets for the biological, ecological, social, economic and environmental sustainability of natural resources. it also integrates the fundamental elements of the common fisheries policy in terms of maximum sustainable yield and the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. in view of the common interest in the development and proper use of living marine resources in the mediterranean and black sea, and the conservation and sustainable use of marine resources and the protection of marine ecosystems, it is recommended that parliament give its consent to the conclusion of this modified agreement, which i personally support.

madam president, every year the european commission publishes a report on the protection of the financial interests of the european union. the aim is to prevent fraud and promote sound financial management. the commission also notes that the 2013 report on the financial corrections of the european union to the general budget of the union for the financial year 2013 was published in the official journal of the european union on 29 march 2013. this may indicate that the detection system is working better, but it also points to the need for more effective prevention measures. i supported this report which calls for greater cooperation between member states and the european commission to increase transparency and accountability and to tackle corruption, organised crime, tax evasion and tax avoidance in order to minimise the negative financial impact of fraud and irregularities.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the 2013 annual report on the protection of the eu's financial interests: fight against fraud, as it is vital to ensure the proper management and efficient use of eu funds. i fully support the fight against corruption, fraud, money laundering and any other illegal activities detrimental to the financial interests of the union, the allocation of additional resources to combat such activities, and the principles of accountability and transparency. in this regard, greater and structured coordination between member states, anti-corruption bodies, managing authorities and the european commission is needed, as well as the exchange of good practices to harmonise the approach to fight corruption. the commission should be able to verify that the information provided by the member states is accurate and that the information provided by the member states is correct. the quality of protection of the eu's financial interests enhances citizens' trust in the european institutions and contributes to the achievement of the union's objectives and policies.
written. ‒ given the current economic difficulties faced by the member states and the lack of resources in the eu budget, the protection of the financial interests of the european union is particularly important. in 2013, a total of 15 779 irregularities were reported to the commission for a total amount of approximately eur 2,14 billion, of which approximately eur 1,76 billion related to expenditure of the eu budget, representing 1,34% of all payments, and the remaining eur 380 million representing 1,86% of the gross accumulated traditional own resources. the recovery rate for fraud cases in 2013 was only 23,74%, which is below the average level of 33,5%. the direct loss of customs revenue caused by cigarette smuggling is estimated at more than eur 10 billion per year. the commission and the member states are both obliged to do everything in their power to combat fraud, corruption and any other illegal activity affecting the financial interests of the union. the protection of the financial interests of the eu, together with the principle of sound financial management, should ensure that budget revenue and expenditure contribute to the fulfilment of the eu's priorities and objectives and to building greater trust among citizens by convincing them that their money is used in accordance with the eu's objectives and policies and in the interest of the eu citizens.
written. ‒ i support the report by mr pirinsky because the protection of the financial interests of the european union is particularly important and the financial resources allocated to the functioning of the eu must be properly managed and used in a meaningful way. investigating and reporting financial irregularities and fraud is an important segment of the fight, and therefore this report has strong implications for further work. the detection of fraud in the cohesion policy segment of the eu budget shows where funds are going wrongly. the new control of cohesion policy planning will prevent and reduce the risk of irregularities. the european anti-fraud office (olaf) has the most important role to play in protecting and controlling revenue and expenditure, i.e. in combating irregularities in the spending of funds. its further work will significantly reduce financial fraud in the eu. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the budget and the implementation of the budgetary and financial management. the commission should also strongly advocate a strict policy on termination and suspension. each member state of the union is obliged to appoint, by the end of 2014, an anti-fraud coordination office which will strengthen olaf's cooperation with the member states.
written. ‒ i supported the report on the 2013 annual report on the protection of the eu's financial interests, as the protection of the eu's financial interests and the fight against fraud should ensure that budget revenue and expenditure contribute to the fulfilment of the eu's priorities and objectives, but also to building up citizens' trust. the commission has also been asked to provide a report on the implementation of the new law on corruption and to provide a report on the implementation of the new law on corruption and corruption. the report showed that fraud was 38 percent less in 2013 but that the number of irregularities reported increased by 16 percent compared to the same year. it is particularly interesting that cigarettes, as the most and most easily smuggled product, have caused significant revenue losses to the budgets of the eu and its member states. the direct loss of customs revenue caused by cigarette smuggling is estimated at more than eur 10 billion per year. in the light of the above, i consider that improved cooperation between the member states and the commission is necessary in order to ensure appropriate measures to avoid and correct irregularities and i therefore call on the member states to demonstrate strong political will in the fight against corruption.
written. ‒ the the annual report underlines the obligation of both the commission and the member states to do everything in their power to combat all other forms of illegal activities affecting the financial interests of the union, in accordance with the provisions of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the commission should be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 290 tfeu concerning the establishment of a european data protection supervisor. the protection of the financial interests of the union, in the area of resources and expenditure, requires an equal level of vigilance. i welcome the report because 98% of the traditional own funds were raised without significant problems and the reported irregularities considered as fraudulent amounted to 0,29% of the gross established traditional own funds (worth eur 61 million) while the irregularities not considered as fraudulent amounted to 1,57% of the traditional own funds (worth eur 327,4 million). this report refers to the ongoing work on improving gni data and to the issues raised in the thematic report of the european court of auditors 11/2013 that require a shorter, more focused audit of gni amounts and improved reporting and coordination of results in order to make the gni system more reliable in contributing to the calculation of eu revenue.
written. the report helps to identify the areas most at risk of fraud by allowing for more precise identification of anti-fraud measures both at eu-wide and national level. this year, the report is largely based on the progress made by member states in developing the national anti-corruption coordination services that had to be established in relation to olaf regulations. the aim of these services is to work closely with olaf in order to join forces to fight fraud. the report welcomes the efforts made by the commission to protect the financial interests of the union and stresses that the fight against corruption can only be achieved through better, more accountable and transparent cooperation between all services. i therefore support this report.

vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy.– mr president, i would like to thank this chamber for the chance to discuss here today something that is extremely serious. i believe, as do you, that we all shared a sense of not only sadness, but also indignation, when we learned on the evening of 27 february of the murder of boris nemtsov in moscow. he was killed just two days before leading a demonstration against the war in ukraine and the effects of the economic crisis in russia. on sunday last week, tens of thousands of citizens in moscow, but also in other cities, turned these marches into a tribute to a man who served his country as a deputy prime minister in the 1990s and who since then had relentlessly tried to bring his country forward. all 28 european union ambassadors, together with our european union head of delegation, were united in attending his funeral on tuesday, joining an impressive crowd. let me share here the words expressed by president schulz on russia’s refusal to let one of you, ms kalniete, into russia to attend his funeral. the same also happened to other representatives of european union member states. this goes against the spirit of our visa facilitation agreement and follows similar incidents that have happened already. i remember when ms harms and mr landsbergis received a similar refusal to enter the country. they joined the words of the president of the european parliament in saying that this is simply not acceptable. we shall remember boris as a strong advocate for a modern, democratic and open russia – a russia open to the world. he defended values which we all share: respect for human dignity; commitments to democracy and to accountability; belief in civil society as a force. he was opposed to war in ukraine, and he was gathering evidence on the involvement of russian troops. yesterday, here in strasbourg in this parliament, i met with mikhail kasyanov, who shared his political commitment. for me, it was a way to honour his memory and to express, once again, our sadness at the loss that his family, friends and his colleagues have suffered, and for the gap he leaves in political life in russia. but it also gave me a chance to discuss the state of democracy in russia. russian citizens deserve no less than a democratic and open russia. strengthening political freedoms and supporting the consolidation of democracy are, moreover, objectives set out in the first article of the partnership and cooperation agreement between the european union and russia. we support russian organisations who are working on improving the legal framework in russia. in our human rights consultations, we have called on russia – time and again – to establish a level playing field for political parties by allowing opposition parties to play a role and by ensuring diversity of the media. looking at the state of democracy in russia today, we see that freedom of expression is under increased pressure. opposition parties struggle to exist and to have access to mainstream media. some have been repeatedly denied registration. the last duma elections in 2011 were described as ‘slanted in favour of the ruling party’ by osce/odihr. remember that the russian population opposed those practices by taking to the streets, leading to the well—known bolotnaya square trials. individual leaders who emerged from those events are constantly harassed, while others left russia out of fear for their freedom or for their lives. this recent assassination brings back to our minds the memories of many others: natalia estemirova, anna politkovskaya, stanislav markelov, anastasia baburova, sergei magnitsky and alexander litvinenko. journalists, lawyers, intelligence officers, human rights defenders – they had little in common until they became victims of those who portray so—called ‘enemies of the state’ as legitimate targets. we all know that the conflict in ukraine has intensified the public discourse against the too—famous fifth column. let us not forget those who face trial in russia through unfair procedures because of the ukrainian conflict, such as nadia savchenko and oleg sentsov, who was arrested in crimea. the russian authorities have not only the duty to conduct a full and transparent investigation into the murder of boris nemtsov, but they also have to put an end to the climate of suspicion, hatred and intolerance for diversity of opinion. the defence of basic freedoms, including the freedom of expression, is – i would like to remind you in this room – a statutory obligation for all members of the united nations.

mr president, i support this report in the majority, but as a representative from croatia i feel obliged to respond to paragraph 165 of the report in which the rapporteur expresses regret over the outcome of the croatian referendum on the definition of marriage in december 2013. i think there is no reason to regret, because the constitutional definition of marriage in croatia has not in any way harmed the rights of the lgbt community. that's right. it served as a catalyst for the passage of the same-sex life partnership law in july 2014 that placed the same-sex community within the law as befits a society that cares for all its members. the desire of the vast majority of croatian citizens to keep marriage as a union between one man and one woman is not an expression of homophobia or discrimination as point 165 of the report imputes. it is a call to protect the traditional values that have kept our society homogeneous despite the frequent historical disasters that have affected croatia.
mr president, the annual human rights report is an important instrument for guiding the european union's foreign policy and development cooperation policy. this report must focus on the human rights situation outside the eu and therefore i hope that the sentences on the member states will eventually be deleted from the resolution, because they have no place here. we also need to follow more systematically the european union charter of fundamental rights, which puts the right to life at the forefront of human rights promotion. this question is often put in the context of ideological struggles or worldviews. but the fact is that 21st-century science proves that human life begins long before birth, at conception. we have left the regulation of human life and reproductive health to the member states, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity. the same principle should apply in relations with non-eu countries we must not impose on other peoples solutions that are rightly rejected by non-european peoples in general as an ideology of waste and disregard for the fundamental right to life. human rights are universal, but only when it is really just about the right of a human being to live in dignity from conception to death - everything else would be an expression of ideological arrogance.

vice-president of the commission. – madam president, first of all, i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr landsbergis and the committee on international trade (inta) for their valuable work on this report and for expediting approval procedures. i would also like to thank the committee on foreign affairs (afet) for its contribution. as you know, the commission submitted its proposal for a macro-financial assistance operation for ukraine in the context of the enormous political and security challenges in ukraine, and a deteriorating economic situation. ukraine is confronted by deep recession: its currency has depreciated strongly, inflation has been rising and international reserves have been declining. this shows that the situation is very acute, and ukraine badly needs international financial assistance as soon as possible. indeed, international donors led by the imf have wrapped up a new financial aid package for ukraine, with the most recent imf extended fund facility, of 11 march 2015, amounting to usd 17.5 billion. the eu is also contributing with its current commission proposal for macro-financial assistance (mfa) of eur 1.8 billion in addition to the previous mfa operations of eur 1.6 billion in loans. it is intended that this mfa operation will be disbursed in three equal tranches, and this is going to be the highest amount of assistance ever disbursed to a third country in such a short period of time. of course, a new mfa operation will be subject to the fulfilment of conditions, namely political preconditions concerning respect for democratic mechanisms, human rights and the rule of law. moreover, ukraine must satisfactorily implement the imf programme and, last but not least, must fulfil economic and financial policy conditions to be agreed between the eu and ukraine in a memorandum of understanding. in this context, potential policy measures in the areas of public finance management, anti-corruption and transparency, the business environment, energy sector reform and financial sector reform are being explored and will be discussed with our ukrainian partners. i would stress that timing is of the essence here. ukraine’s most urgent and important financing needs are in 2015, and the first two of the three tranches under the newly proposed mfa operation should be disbursed this year – i.e. the first tranche before the summer break in mid-2015. contrary to its proposal for last year’s mfa operation of eur 1 billion, which was based on the urgency procedure, with a council decision as provided for in article 213 of the treaty, the commission has based the present proposal on article 212 of the treaty, which provides for a decision under the ordinary legislative procedure. the current commission proposal follows precisely established practice for mfa operations – practice also reflected in the joint declaration of parliament and the council of 12 august 2013 on granting mfa. in view of ukraine’s urgent financial needs, swift adoption of the current proposal by the co-legislators under the ordinary legislative procedure is very important. therefore, i am pleased that the international trade and foreign affairs committees upheld the commission proposal without amendments. i am also pleased that the council, through coreper, today agreed to adopt the commission’s proposal without amendments.
