written. ‒ as the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was established to provide support for workers made redundant and self-employed persons who have ceased their activity as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns caused by globalisation, the prolonged global financial and economic crisis referred to in regulation (ec) no 546/2009 (3) or the new global financial and economic crisis, and to help them reintegrate into the labour market, i support the allocation of eur 5 046 000 in commitment and payment appropriations to partly finance redundancy losses in 16 enterprises falling under section 60 of the nace rev. 2 classification of programmes (issuance). member states should show solidarity with each other when necessary, and i am glad that they have shown this today by this example.
the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was established to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market and find a new job. at the same time, union financial assistance to workers made redundant should be dynamic and available as quickly and efficiently as possible. the greek authorities submitted an application for a financial contribution from the egf in respect of the project egf/2014/018 gr/attica broadcasting following the redundancies of 928 workers in 16 enterprises in the broadcasting sector. according to the greek authorities, the economy has been in a deep recession for the last six years (2008 to 2013), and according to elstat, the greek statistical body, since 2008 greek gdp has decreased by 25,7 percentage points; public consumption by 21 percentage points and private consumption by 32,3 percentage points, while unemployment has increased by 20,6 percentage points. the commission notes that the greek authorities have not provided any evidence that the restructuring plan is in line with the restructuring plan. i therefore support the report of rapporteur georgios kyrtsos on the mobilisation of eur 5 046 000, representing 60% of the total cost, as the objective is to help displaced workers to train and re-qualify for new jobs.

member of the commission.– madam president, i fully share your concern about the need to work together to address alcohol-related harm (arh) across the european union. at this stage, i wish to express my regret that commissioner andriukaitis is not able to be here this evening, but i am glad to be able to take this debate on his behalf. alcohol is a killer and each year 120 000 eu citizens die from alcohol-related harm. the term ‘alcohol-related harm’ covers more than 60 types of diseases and conditions, including: addiction; injuries; liver, cardiovascular and mental diseases; and certain cancers. so it affects not only the individual drinker, but also many other people, particularly family members. drink-driving, violence and the suffering of children and families with alcohol problems are all part of the bigger picture of the harm that alcohol abuse inflicts on society. europe is still the world’s number one alcohol drinker, with an annual average of over 10 litres of pure alcohol per person and with significant variation among member states, regions and population groups, and yet most alcohol-related harm can be avoided. the commission is therefore keen to find the best way to work together with all stakeholders to deliver concrete results and to reduce alcohol-related harm. we therefore envisage shaping a framework of action to which the commission, the member states, parliament and civil society can all contribute. all our efforts need to be truly joined up and all of us have an important role to play. of course, the member states have the main competence and responsibility to address harmful alcohol consumption, for example by setting and enforcing age limits and regulating accessibility. just last week at the informal meeting of health ministers, member states expressed support for an eu approach to address alcohol-related harm. the commission is indeed ready to do its part to support national efforts and, as such, the commission intends to build on the solid foundations of the 2006 eu alcohol strategy and maintain its objectives and tools to work together with stakeholders. when i speak about the necessary tools i mean the european alcohol and health forum as well as the committee on national alcohol policy in action, and the joint action we currently have with member states to reduce alcohol-related harm. along with the renewed eu health policy forum, these tools can help secure the active involvement of all stakeholders, and in this way we can ensure that all efforts are unified and mutually reinforcing. in addition to alcohol-related harm, we need to carefully consider alcohol labelling. i want to confirm to mr la via that the commission has started preparatory work on a report about the possible use of ingredient lists and nutrition information for alcoholic beverages. further discussions are, however, needed before we can announce a date for the adoption of this report. at the same time, i believe that we need to focus more on health promotion and disease prevention and place action on the main causes of chronic diseases – not only in relation to alcohol but also in connection with tobacco, nutrition and physical inactivity – into a wider context; in other words, we need a holistic approach to preventing chronic diseases. whether or not the paper or instrument that enshrines such action is called a strategy is not in itself important. what matters most is not the tool that we use or its name, but the achievement of positive results and outcomes. i am confident that the european parliament, the member states, the commission and civil society, by working together, can succeed in reducing alcohol-related harm and, as such, contribute towards a healthier europe.

written. ‒ fishing is the activity with the highest percentage of accidents at work, with as many as 24 000 people dying every year while fishing. this is alarming evidence that indicates the need for significantly better protection of fishermen in the course of their activities. the international convention on standards of training, certification and watchkeeping for personnel on fishing vessels (stcw-f convention) was adopted by the international maritime organisation (imo) in london on 7 july 1995 by 74 states, 22 of which are now members of the european union. however, only four member states (spain, denmark, latvia and lithuania) have ratified the stcw-f convention. this is also because, under eu regulations, the eu must give its consent to the member states for ratification. i therefore support the consent of the council to the authorisation of member states to become parties, in the interest of the union, to the international convention on standards of training, certification and watchkeeping for personnel on fishing vessels of the international maritime organisation. i believe this decision is the right step forward to better protect our fishermen and i hope that similar protection standards will soon be applicable to all fishermen, regardless of the length and strength of the vessels they sail on.

in writing. – i voted in favour of the recommendation on the international convention on standards of training, certification and watch keeping for fishing vessel personnel, signed in 1995, as it will allow member states to ratify the convention without infringing on the eu's executive competence in regards to the ‘recognition of regulated professions pursed by eu nationals on board fishing vessels'. the importance of this convention is evident as the highest accident rates occur when fishing- approximately of 24 000 lives are lost, per year, in fishing incidents. the recommendation supports a convention that aims at helping ensure safety measures for all life and property on sea. the countries that signed the stcw-f convention in 1995 are to ensure mandatory training for personnel using vessels that are 24 meters or more in length, while countries who did not sign the convention are encouraged to do so as its training requirements will ensure that the personnel using fishing vessels are qualified to do so- the qualification entails an official certificate accompanied by a medical certificate. furthermore, the signatory countries are not obliged, but encouraged to adapt laws that will require training and certification standards for smaller vessels, or vessels of less strength, as it will help minimise the high number of accidents that occur at sea.

written. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the council position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 223/2009 on european statistics, in view of the importance of statistical data for policy-making, the need to adopt measures to improve the credibility of statistical data, the independence of the statistical institutions, the management of statistics, european coordination with national statistics and their co-responsibility.
written. ‒ statistical data must be accurate, true, comprehensive and comparable. they monitor developments in the member states, compare countries with each other and define recommendations for necessary reforms, with the aim of achieving shared growth and development. in practice, there have been instances of attempts to hide or misrepresent statistical data, sometimes due to lack of knowledge of the methodology, and sometimes deliberately with the aim of concealing shortcomings in the functioning of the state and the economy. such actions are subject to penalties and statistical systems must not be subject to political decision-making. i supported the report on the amendment of the legal framework for european statistics, as it insists on strengthening the independence of the national statistical authorities while pointing out the high degree of responsibility they have. it is requested that specific measures be established per member state to improve the national statistical system and to comply with the european statistics code of practice. the legal framework for the wider use of administrative data for the production of european statistics is also established. the main objective of this amendment is to further strengthen the european statistical system, its independence and the production of high-quality data which are a key basis for decision-making and good governance. that is why i supported this report on european statistics.
written. ‒ the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 223/2009 on european statistics (05161/2/2015 c8-0073/2015 2012/0084 ((cod)) will strengthen the professional independence of the national statistical authorities and the credibility of statistics. the reliability of statistical data is a prerequisite for ensuring the confidence of users, and the credibility of the institutions responsible for producing statistics is equally important. this regulation calls for a revision of the existing underlying legal framework for european statistics, adapting it to meet the needs and challenges of policy-making for european statistics in the light of recent developments in the world economy. the regulation also refers specifically to the heads of the national statistical offices as persons whose independence in the performance of their duties is a prerequisite for establishing the independence of the institutions concerned and includes the establishment of an 'obligation of confidence in statistics'. in view of the above and given the high likelihood of positive effects of this regulation, i support the proposal for a regulation and the council's position.
written. ‒ i support the positive report by mr bayet on the council position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 223/2009 on european statistics, following the recommendations and opinions of the european central bank of 6 november 2012 and of the spanish congress of deputies and senate and the austrian federal council, submitted under protocol no 2 on the application of the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality, which states that the draft legislative act is not in line with the principle of subsidiarity.
written. ‒ it is essential to continue work on strengthening the professional independence of national statistical authorities in order to ensure the full credibility of statistical data at member state level, but also at eu level. to that end, it is necessary to define in the amended regulation measures that achieve the legally guaranteed independence of statistical authorities, prevent political pressure and guarantee the highest standards of statistical data processing. it is therefore good that the statistical authorities of the member states will not be able to seek or receive instructions from national political authorities through their heads. it is equally important to ensure the independence of the statistical system at european level. the statistical office of the european communities (eurostat) is indispensable for the european institutions to be able to take quality and informed decisions at all stages and levels of their work. reliability of statistics is also rightly sought through a stronger european statistical system - the coordination of eurostat, the national statistical institutes and other national statistical authorities. for all these reasons, i welcome the commission proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 223/2009 on european statistics, support the council's position at first reading and the recommendation of the bayet rapporteur.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the governance of the european statistical system (ess) needs to be strengthened by ensuring the unconditional application of the principle of professional independence of the national statistical institute (nsis), by clarifying its role as coordinator in the national statistical systems and by increasing the use of administrative data for statistical purposes. the proposal calls for a revision of the existing underlying legal framework for european statistics, adapting it to the policy needs and challenges created for european statistics by recent developments in the global economy. the main objective is to further strengthen governance in the european statistical system in order to safeguard high credibility and to respond appropriately to the data needs arising from the enhanced coordination of economic policies in the european union.
written. i supported this proposal as it will ensure a higher quality and credibility of statistical data in the member states of the european union on the basis of which, ultimately, we in the european parliament and the european commission make our decisions. it is of particular importance that member states establish national authorities responsible for carrying out statistical analyses to ensure that their credibility is not undermined. i consider it even more important to apply and standardise the methodology when processing data, and for this to happen all the member states' institutions and other state bodies responsible for this must be coordinated. i believe that eurostat must remain an independent body that will guarantee effective supervision of all the statistical offices of the member states, all in order to give citizens of the union easy access to data. the adoption of the report will ensure up-to-date and credible statistics in all member states, which will also allow investors to efficiently access the necessary information, which may lead to an increase in investment in the member states of the union.
mr president, the marine strategy framework directive is a comprehensive and demanding act that is crucial in implementing a coordinated policy of the member states with the aim of sustainable management of the marine environment based on an ecosystem approach. the management of commercial stocks and of species that are subject to by-catch is crucial for the sustainability of ecosystems. at a time when the fishing opportunities far outweigh the ecological balance and the catch is greater than the potential for natural recovery of the species, without respecting the ecosystem approach to fisheries management we will not achieve the desired objectives of good environmental status by 2020, nor ensure sustainability in this important frontier economy that should ensure future generations the benefits we enjoy today.
written. ‒ i support this report, as it is the first multiannual plan under the reformed common fisheries policy and as such will also serve as a model for other upcoming multiannual plans in fisheries. the plan aims to ensure the sustainable exploitation of cod, herring and mackerel stocks in the baltic sea and to ensure the stability of fisheries in accordance with all aspects of ecosystem and environmental protection.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a multiannual plan for the cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea and the fisheries exploiting those stocks, amending council regulation (ec) no 2187/2005 and repealing council regulation (ec) no 1098/2007. this is an important multiannual management plan that takes into account multiple species that are interconnected and interact. it is also important because these three species - cod, herring and papalina in the baltic sea - account for over 94% of catches in recent years, and there are risks of overfishing and the consequences for the ecosystem of the baltic sea's closure. such a plan may serve to develop other management and exploitation plans for fish stocks in other seas and for fish that interact with each other.
‒ 94% of the total baltic fisheries catch is cod, herring and sprat. this report aims to ensure a balanced exploitation of the stock, taking into account the interaction and impact of these three species on each other and the sustainability of the entire ecosystem. i support the report by mr wałęsa, who agrees with the commission's proposal that a management plan for all fisheries in the baltic sea is needed because this approach is more efficient. such a plan should ensure optimum exploitation of the catch and the stability of the fisheries in the baltic sea. detailed scientific research is needed to establish the current state of the baltic sea fish species, their role in the ecosystem and to determine the period during which fishing is prohibited. as this is a long process, we can conclude that this is just the beginning of creating a single marine ecosystem management plan, which should be an example for other seas.

written. ‒ i support the multiannual plan for fisheries in the baltic sea. the reports on the current state of fish species and their interrelations in the ecosystem show that there is a need to revise the rules adopted in 2009. a plan is needed that has three priority points: 1. the biological relationship between the three main species of fish: cod, herring and parrotfish; 2. the exact determination of the maximum catch that does not threaten the reproductive stock units; and 3. the catch determined by the time period. in addition to the above criteria, it is good that proposals have been suggested for the implementation of measures for the detailed monitoring of fisheries species in the baltic sea with a strong oversight by the bsac.
written. ‒ i supported a multiannual plan for cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea and the fisheries exploiting those stocks. the union has a conservation obligation, including the maintenance or restoration of populations of harvested species at levels that can produce the highest sustainable yield. the objective is to establish a fisheries plan for a large number of species taking into account the dynamics between the cod, herring and sprat stocks and the input of species in the fisheries to those stocks, i.e. plaice, mackerel, herring and plaice in the baltic. the objective of that plan should be to restore, achieve and maintain populations of the species concerned above levels that can produce the highest sustainable yield for the stocks concerned while minimising the impact on other species such as seabirds and on the wider marine environment.
written. fishing is one of the main economic activities of most of the baltic states. it is subject to the influence of various biotic and abiotic factors which condition its unfolding and direct its development. the correct management and protection of the renewable resources of the sea requires that account be taken of the biotechnological, technical, economic, legal and all other aspects which have a decisive influence on the development of fisheries. in recent years, there has been a massive poaching of juveniles, threatening the diversity of the species and devastating the undersea environment. cod, herring and sprat are important fisheries in the baltic sea. the current exploitation rates for some of those stocks are not in line with the achievement of the maximum sustainable yield and it is necessary to find the best possible solution that will ensure the sustainable exploitation of the stocks without harming fishermen by introducing unrealistic quotas. i therefore support the proposal to establish a management plan for cod, herring and papalina stocks in the baltic, as the plan should ensure sustainable fisheries while taking account of biological and environmental benefits. it is therefore necessary to cooperate with the profession and to base management on the latest scientific information.
written. ‒ i supported the report on the establishment of a multiannual plan for cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea and the fisheries exploiting those stocks, as i believe it properly sets out the framework for the management of those stocks. this is necessary because these three species account for more than 94% of the catches in the baltic sea in recent years. in addition, this regulation is very important as these three species are continuously interacting in the baltic sea and it is therefore useful to recognise the impact of cod on herring and parrot stocks and vice versa. in particular, i support the fact that this report does not grant any new powers to the commission beyond those set out in the basic regulation, but gives the member states concerned the possibility to make recommendations in order to agree on appropriate solutions in accordance with their current situations.
written. ‒ i support this report which is a compromise and gives fishermen the opportunity to adapt, after which it will be sanctioned to throw unwanted catches back into the sea. in any case, efforts should be made to eliminate this harmful behaviour of fishermen at sea, and landing sites for such fish are one way to address this problem. we must take account of the needs of fishermen to enable them to do their jobs successfully, but also take care to protect marine flora and fauna.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulations (ec) no 850/98, (ec) no 2187/2005, (ec) no 1967/2006, (ec) no 1098/2007, (ec) no 254/2002, (ec) no 2347/2002 and (ec) no 1224/2009 and repealing regulation (ec) no 1434/98 as regards the landing obligation, although i consider that such a proposal is very difficult to apply in particular to small fishermen, but i want to believe that both landings also mean sustainability in fisheries. i support the proposed amendments as the amended proposal also introduces a transitional period for the full implementation of the landing obligation and introduces selectivity and flexibility in its implementation. i believe that other regulations to help fishermen will follow the commissioner's discussion. the aim is to end the practice of discarding fish and to contribute to the conservation of the marine ecosystem, eliminating unwanted or unnecessary catches along the way. the ultimate aim is to strengthen the fisheries in the long term.
written. ‒ these changes represent a step forward towards the efficient and sustainable use of the marine ecosystem. the new regulation will introduce an obligation for fishermen to land and store 'inadvertent catches' (catches below the reference minimum) and breach of this obligation would be characterised as a serious infringement. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fishing opportunities for bluefin tuna are not reduced. the commission has also proposed to amend the fishing opportunities for norway lobster in the baltic sea, in particular by introducing a new fishing zone for norway lobster in the baltic sea. since they are exempt, i supported this report.
the reform of the common fisheries policy adopted in 2013 brought about fundamental changes to the rules applicable to fisheries. the commission considers that the exemption from the landing obligation is justified by the fact that the landing obligation is not applicable to the species concerned. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 26 to amend this regulation by supplementing it with new rules. as this landing obligation regulation conflicts with several existing eu regulations currently in force, the commission requested the amendment of seven regulations to bring them into line with the regulation of the basic common fisheries policy. the landing obligation represents a radical change for fisheries and 2015 will therefore be a test year for the implementation of this change, from which messages for further application should be drawn. the commission has also provided for an adjustment period of two years during which infringements of the landing obligation will not be considered as serious infringements.
written. ‒ according to the un, a quarter of all fish caught in the european union is discarded, the most in the world, because it is not the species that the fishing fleets wanted to catch. the way that member countries dispose of surplus fish has for years been a source of outrage to the public and to environmental organizations. the problem is particularly acute in northern europe. there, fishermen target certain species, and others that they don't have a quota or a license for, and they find themselves in their nets, they throw them into the sea. you don't catch a lot of unwanted fish in croatia. we have in the cage catch maybe ten to twenty percent of that catch, in the swimming pool almost nothing, and in the other nets and so on that catch is quite negligible. regardless, while we limit small fishermen to catching any fish for personal use, the big ones throw tons of unwanted fish back into the sea. this system is absolutely unacceptable, which is why i support the new proposal to harmonise european regulations on this issue and i hope that it will really lead to a reduction in the amount of fish discarded.
written. ‒ i support the obligation to land catches in order to ensure that the existing rules are applied as much as possible and to reduce catches and conserve fish stocks. this application is of particular importance to me as a representative from croatia, where the lives of many fishing families are directly linked to the regulation and enforcement of overfishing regulations. the implementation of technical measures in fisheries and controls is key to sustainable development and to prevent further fishing.
written. ‒ i supported the european parliament resolution on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the landing obligation. the basic objective of the regulation is to progressively eliminate discards in all fisheries in the european union by introducing an obligation to land catches of species subject to catch limits and of species covered by minimum sizes in the mediterranean sea. in order to make the landing obligation operational for the catches of the species covered by it as from 1 january 2015, certain provisions under the current regulations concerning technical and control measures which are contrary to the landing obligations and which require fishermen to discard fish need to be deleted or amended.
written. i supported the commission's proposal on landing catches as it is complementary to the european parliament's proposal of february 2013 on the progressive implementation of landings with a view to reducing waste and preserving marine flora and fauna, which entered into force in the member states on 1 january 2015. the commission should also be able to assess the impact of the proposed measures on the union's fishing fleet and on the union's fishing industry. the commission should be able to assess the impact of the landing obligation on the fishermen concerned, taking into account the impact of the landing obligation on the fishermen concerned. i therefore believe that a step-by-step approach and gradual adaptation of legislation can make a more significant contribution to the success of this regulation, namely the achievement of the ultimate objective of protecting the blue economy and protecting our seas.

mr president, the main message of this report is that the bologna process needs to be reformed and new models of education developed, which i fully agree with. the bologna process started in 1999 and is now being implemented in the 47 countries that make up the european higher education area. it was introduced with the aim of raising the quality and standardisation of higher education, and allows for the recognition of qualifications and diplomas and the mobility of students and professors. it is the exchange of knowledge, experience and practice at different universities that is the best way to improve quality. when we draw a line today and look at the results of 15 years of work on the bologna process, we see positive changes in terms of better organisation of higher education and the possibility of comparing education systems in the member states. but a major shortcoming still exists, and that is the lack of connection with the needs of the labour market. that's why we need urgent changes.
written. ‒ i support this report by ms łybacke, as an initiative in the run-up to the upcoming ministerial conference in yerevan on 14-15 may. while there have been many achievements in the areas of implementation of the bologna process, there are large disparities in its implementation across participating countries. given that youth unemployment is the biggest problem in the eu, i think it is extremely important that the european parliament sends a clear message to the forthcoming conference in yerevan, so that we can take a stronger stance on youth and thus contribute to a better and more quality education for young people in the future.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of the bologna process monitoring report because i support the accompanying analysis of the situation, the numerous initiatives and proposals, the priorities and challenges it sets out, and the prominent role of the bologna process. harmonised, transparent, quality higher education is crucial for cultural, economic and social development, and the bologna objectives should ensure the achievement and realisation of a successful european higher education in the current challenges of modern development. in this context, it is necessary, inter alia, to take a realistic view of the situation, the achievement of the objectives and the accelerating changes in society and the economy, to strengthen links with research and development, to promote the possibilities of applying new technologies and, in addition, to coordinate the operation of european programmes supporting the bologna process.
written. ‒ the report focuses on the importance of making the most of the available resources and finding new funding models and reviving the bologna process in its important role in the revision of the europe 2020 strategy, as well as in the juncker investment plan for europe. improving the quality of higher education and establishing quality assurance systems is a high priority for many countries. the european standards and guidelines for quality assurance and the key objective of the european higher education area have been revised and are subject to approval by the ministerial conference in may 2015. my assessment is that the success of the bologna process is partial, the recognition of diplomas and the mobility of young people is the greatest success achieved by this process, but the process is also characterised by the emergence of new higher education institutions and programmes that have failed to provide adequate quality education. this is confirmed by the fact that we have more and more highly educated young people who cannot find their place in the labour market. the european commission has published a report on the implementation of the european social fund's work programme for the period 2007-2013.
written. ‒ coherent, transparent and quality higher education is essential for cultural, economic and social development. the objectives of the bologna process provide essential means for european higher education to successfully face the current challenges. however, there is still a long way to go to achieve these goals. for example, the system of recognition of higher education diplomas between member states is not yet fully implemented, so croatian citizens, for example, face difficulties in recognising their qualifications in certain eu member states. it is important that the upcoming ministerial conference in yerevan in may 2015 provides an objective and critical overview of the progress and setbacks in achieving the 2012-2015 priorities with a view to further consolidating the ehea and strengthening the bologna process.
written. ‒ i support the report by ms łybacke on the need to monitor and analyse the implementation of the bologna process. the launch of the bologna process in 1999 gave added meaning to the european project which has since sought a more integrated and harmonised education system among the countries of the european higher education area. i expect a good assessment of the results achieved over the past 15 years, particularly in terms of competitiveness and employability of graduates, mobility, guarantees of recognition of academic achievements and the uneven application of the bologna system in the member states. the first moves of the new juncker commission put the focus on measures for growth and employment, especially for young people, of whom some 5 million in the eu are still out of work. the bologna system should be upgraded in the coming period through the objectives of this resolution. the biggest challenge for national governments is to adapt education systems to the real needs of the labour market and to offer young people skills that can lead to jobs. it is important that the seven-year eu financial framework does not reduce development funding for education, innovation and research, in particular that provided for under horizon 2020, in order to achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. i also believe that support is necessary for countries such as croatia, where the bologna system is being revised, because in recent years there has been no greater recognition of first-year qualifications by employers.
written. ‒ i supported the report on the follow-up to the bologna process because it is one of the fundamental public policies aimed at strengthening the european spirit and creating european citizenship. unfortunately, in most member states, this cleverly conceived policy is not being successfully implemented. the exchange of knowledge and education of young people, as well as the different educational experiences of young people, are key elements on the way to successful and long-term economic development. the croatian market does not know the real difference between a bachelor's and a master's degree and in 90 percent of cases graduated bachelors are not recognized in the labor market, therefore they continue with an additional degree of education. education is one of the main pillars of our society, so i call on the european and national authorities to provide more administrative and financial support to the process.
written. ‒ i supported the resolution on monitoring the implementation of the bologna process, which calls on member states to further improve and update the assessment of higher education institutions against standards previously established within education systems at international level, and which reward excellence in order to advance knowledge, research and science. it is important to preserve the diversity of teaching, including linguistic diversity, and to encourage member states to increase scholarships and ensure their easy availability.
the bologna declaration is the foundation for the harmonisation of education systems in european countries, signed in june 1999 with the aim of creating a european higher education area (ehea) by 2010. it succeeded, but not completely. i must give the example of croatia, where all universities operate on the "bologna" basis and where progress has been made in the structure of higher education, coordination and quality and student mobility, but not enough care is taken to recruit teaching assistants and non-teaching staff, there is not enough financial resources and equipment, international cooperation is not sufficiently developed, and the division of the four largest universities makes it difficult to clearly define the mission and policy of future development. all these problems have a significant impact on the quality of the university's work. for the reasons stated above, i supported this report because it speaks of maximising the use of eu funds to fully implement the bologna strategy with a view to finding new funding models, and welcomes the fact that president juncker of the european commission has also put emphasis in his investment plan for europe on improving and restoring the quality of higher education.
written. ‒ i supported the report on the monitoring of the implementation of the bologna process, which points to the need to adapt the education system to the labour market, focusing primarily on strengthening skills and knowledge and improving education. as i have already pointed out, i cannot support employment mobility, because the emigration of a workforce certainly cannot have a positive impact in view of the demographic and economic consequences that emigration can have for individual countries, and in particular for the poorer member states, but the mobility of pupils and students for the purpose of acquiring knowledge and training can only represent a positive trend. the effects of the bologna process presented in the report show that the experiences students gain by studying abroad or by carrying out a professional practice certainly contribute to their autonomy, cultural enrichment, knowledge of foreign languages and ability to work in multicultural environments. therefore, i support any form of initiative for young people that will enable them to be educated in the spirit of entrepreneurship and ultimately contribute to a better understanding of the real needs of the market and the shortage of human resources.

member of the commission.– mr president, i would like to thank the members for this discussion. i would not like to give here the impression that the commission is not doing anything. i mentioned that we have several pieces of legislation where other forms of protection for whistle-blowers is included. it was said here that whistle-blowers must be respected because they fulfil a very important task for society, for democracy and for law and that we should protect them; this is also very important. to go back to the luxleaks, which was mentioned several times, i hope you understand that the commission cannot interfere in the member states’ jurisdictions as is the case described here. however, we are taking the necessary measures to increase the transparency on tax rulings. this is a preventive measure to fight tax evasion and tax avoidance which would better protect whistle-blowers. on the european level, we want to introduce measures through which the public will get information in a very transparent way on the advantages that are provided by the member states to companies in the tax sphere. we at the commission have already approved the first step, which is reporting by the member states. this reporting will use a central register, so everybody will see where these tax rulings are adopted. the second step would involve country-by-country reporting, also from the companies themselves. this will be assessed in the course of the next few months to be sure that it will be the most efficient measure to fulfil the purpose, which is transparency and full information provided to european citizens. i believe these preventive steps will also help us fight tax evasion and tax avoidance, and, together with the protection of whistle-blowers at member state level, this can help solve the problems we spoke about here.

‒ council regulation (ec) no 994/98 has been substantially amended. since the commission decided on 1.4.1987 to order that all acts should be codified after a maximum of 10 amendments, a codification of council regulation (ec) no 994/98 of 7 may 1998 on the application of articles 107 and 108 of the tfeu to certain categories of horizontal state aid is necessary. the purpose of this proposal is therefore to codify the said regulation. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the aid is compatible with the internal market. these categories include aid for e.g. small and medium-sized enterprises, environmental protection and research, development and innovation. the commission will assess the compatibility of the aid with the internal market on the basis of the criteria set out in article 107 (3) (c) of the treaty. the commission may also decide to exempt certain aid from the notification procedure laid down in article 108, provided that the aid granted to the same undertaking for a given period does not exceed a fixed amount (de minimis aid). the proposal is indeed limited to the codification of existing texts without any substantial changes, and since i consider that this is an act of great importance, i supported the proposal.

written. ‒ in the interests of clarity and rationality, the commission has tabled this proposal with a view to codifying regulation (ec) no 659/1999 of 22 march 1999 laying down detailed rules for the application of article 108 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the proposal aims to facilitate the review of the content of the acts being codified by making only minor formal changes, but without changing their substance. in accordance with article 108 tfeu, any plans to grant new aid and the necessary information must be notified and submitted by the member states to the commission in good time and may not enter into force before being authorised by the commission. the deadline for the commission to take a decision is two months. this proposal includes a codification of the provisions related to the commission's powers: to request additional information from any member state in case of suspicion of non-compliance of a measure with union rules and to implement compliance measures, where appropriate by means of penalties, to assess the confidentiality of information obtained, to examine data on unlawful aid and to issue 10-year limitations accordingly. the rule on the codification of an act after a dozen amendments, which the commission established in 1987, contributes to greater certainty of the correct application of the act and, for reasons of legal certainty, is in the interest of all those stakeholders to whom these texts will apply, and i have therefore supported this proposal.

written. ‒ the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the monetary funds (com ((2013) 0615 c7-0263/2013 2013/0306 ((cod)) accepts, with certain amendments, the commission's legislative proposal aimed at ensuring uniform supervisory requirements to be applied to the monetary funds throughout the union. the committee on economic and monetary affairs recommended that parliament adopt a first reading position. i agree that it is necessary to adopt a single set of rules in order to avoid a 'contagion' of the short-term financing market that would undermine the stability of the union's financial market. in order to mitigate systemic risk, the proposed regulation lays down the operating conditions of mmfs with fixed net asset value, assets eligible for investment by mmfs and eligible securitisations. i am particularly pleased with the requirements for transparency of investments in mmfs and the proposal for regular weekly information to investors on the activities of the funds in which they have invested their funds. i consider the adoption of this regulation to be very important, particularly from the point of view of the instability of the financial markets, that is, the money market on which money funds also operate. i therefore support this report.
written. ‒ an mmf is a mutual fund that invests in short-term debt, such as money market instruments issued by banks, governments or corporations. the imf is used by a significant proportion of industry, local authorities, charitable foundations, ... as a cash and surplus management instrument, while it provides a significant source of short-term financing: in europe, about 22% of short-term long-term debt securities are held by the government or by the corporate sector by the imf. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 264 concerning the establishment of a european data protection supervisor. furthermore, due to their systemic links to the banking sector and to corporate and government finance, mmfs have been identified as acting in the shadow of banks. these funds are also sensitive to various risks, which is why this proposal for a regulation is on the agenda. this is the second time this proposal has been brought to the econ agenda, as the first attempt failed to reach a compromise, which speaks to the complexity of the area being regulated. the fight to align with the positions of the other political groups, which were mainly to leave the status quo to the unregulated imf, was demanding, but the rapporteur has found a good compromise which is why i want to support her.
written. ‒ i support the report by mrs gill and the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the monetary funds. the emfs provide short-term financing to financial institutions, businesses and governments, which means that they contribute to the financing of the european economy. the important thing is the link between the supply of short-term money and the demand for it. it is therefore important to establish precise, very carefully balanced rules concerning the financial instruments eligible for investment by the mmf, its portfolio and its valuation. it is necessary to lay down reporting requirements in relation to a mmf established, managed or traded in the union. one year after entry into force, only 12 member states had implemented the guidelines for mmfs adopted by the committee of european securities regulators (cesr). it has been shown that differences between national rules still exist and that different national approaches do not address the weaknesses of the money market in the union and that there is no possibility of creating a level playing field. therefore, these common rules for mmfs should address existing problems, provide a high level of investor protection and prevent and mitigate any potential risk of contagion of the short-term funding market and of the mmf sponsor arising from a possible flight from those funds.
written. ‒ monetary funds provide short-term financing to financial institutions, businesses and governments. by financing these entities, the mmfs contribute to the financing of the european economy. such entities use their investments in mmfs as an effective way to spread their own credit risk and credit exposure rather than relying solely on bank deposits. the new rules for mmfs are closely linked to directive 2009/65/ec (the 'mfd directive') and directive 2011/61/eu (the 'mfd directive') as they constitute the legal framework governing the establishment, management and sale of mmfs in the union. the specificity of mmfs derives from the combination of the assets in which they invest and their objectives. the objective of achieving a return in line with money market rates and the objective of preserving the value of investments are not mutually exclusive. the mmf may have one of these objectives or both at the same time. the mmf portfolio rules would require a clear definition of the categories of assets eligible for investment by mmfs and the conditions under which they are eligible. in order to ensure the integrity of mmfs, it is desirable to prohibit certain financial transactions by mmfs that would jeopardise the investment strategy and objectives and thus further destabilise markets in times of instability. so i supported the reporters.
written. mmfs hold monetary instruments such as treasury bills, commercial papers and certificates of deposit, and by trading these instruments in the money market, they provide short-term financing to companies, financial institutions and governments. furthermore, money funds are a key link between the demand for and supply of short-term money in financial markets. although mmfs were considered to be very stable sources of short-term funding, the financial crisis has revealed several features of mmfs that may pose a systemic risk in times of crisis. the commission notes that the bank's capital needs are not limited to the capital needs of the banks, but also to the capital needs of the banks themselves. in order to avoid negative consequences on financial markets, europe needs to set uniform rules across the union, which would make mmfs more resilient to future financial crises and increase investor protection. at the same time, we cannot ignore the important role of monetary funds in financing the state and the corporate sector. it is therefore very important to support the proposal on the monetary funds, as it provides the guidelines for how a united and integrated europe can have a stable and sustainable development of the money market and thus of the economy as a whole.

member of the commission, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy.– madam president, the government of the maldives has taken important steps to enact legislation against domestic violence, human trafficking, the right to information, as well as improving social security, education and health. the european union strongly welcomes these measures. but these gains risk being undermined if the government does not take urgent remedial action to restore the health of its democracy and the sanctity of key democratic principles on which that democracy is founded. the maldives are a fragile and young democracy. since the adoption of the new constitution and the introduction of multiparty elections in 2008, progress has been uneven. notably, there was a disputed and controversial ‘transfer of power’ in february 2012. the ramifications of those events continue to undermine the possibilities for durable progress in the maldives. the arrest of former president nasheed on 22 february this year has exacerbated tensions. mr nasheed was arrested, on charges under the terrorism act, for the alleged kidnapping of the chief justice of the criminal court in 2012. eu heads of missions and the ambassadors of norway and switzerland in colombo issued a statement expressing their concerns about both the arrest and the conduct of the first hearing, which took place without any legal representation. following his conviction and sentencing to 13 years’ imprisonment on 13 march 2015, the european union issued a further statement, raising serious questions about due process of law and the risks of undermining people’s trust in the independence of the judiciary. these statements highlighted the importance of respect for democratic principles, the constitution, the rule of law, due legal process and the independence of the judiciary. i want to take this opportunity to emphasise and reiterate the importance of those principles. these are founding principles of the european union. we remain fully committed to them and convinced of their importance in realising peoples’ legitimate aspirations to democracy throughout the world. the people of the maldives are no different. it is vital that the government takes action now to demonstrate its commitment to the values of freedom of expression and assembly. ensuring that the opposition are able to conduct their activities without harassment by the state is critical to the state of democracy in the maldives. likewise, independent bodies such as the human rights commission and the elections commission have important roles in maintaining democracy. they should be allowed to undertake their constitutionally-mandated roles without fear of sanctions. a free media also has an essential role to play in enabling public scrutiny of the government. the government should seek to remove legal restrictions on the media’s ability to legitimately report and ensure that any attacks on the media are properly and thoroughly investigated and the culprits brought to justice. the vice-president/high representative has welcomed the request from the government of the maldives to send an observer to any appeal by mr nasheed. the vice-president/high representative has offered to send a legal expert, not only to examine the nasheed case, but also to review legislation, the procedures and practices of the judiciary and implementation of the new penal code. we hope this will enable those areas where the respect for rule of law can be enhanced to be highlighted, in line with the stipulations of the 2008 constitution and other relevant laws. on this basis, the maldivian authorities and the european union will have a clear basis for further work to best protect the rule of law in the maldives. these are not idle concerns. already there is evidence that islamic extremists are actively aiming to recruit disaffected maldivians to the nihilism of the jihadist cause. the european union wants to help the maldivian authorities address the underlying causes of radicalisation. but real progress will inevitably depend principally on the government and its prompt and ongoing action to ensure that the political system in the maldives is as healthy as possible.
madam president, when we talk about the maldives, for most people in europe the first image that comes to mind is probably a tourist paradise on earth. however, the local population lives far from such idyll and sees a much darker reality where democratic standards are plummeting. the recent sentencing of the first democratically elected and now former president of the maldives, mohamed nasheed, to 13 years in prison raises serious and justified doubts about the rule of law and institutions in the maldives. only the trial went ahead with numerous objections from un officials. without entering into the guilt or innocence of former president nasheed, because that's not our job, we must insist on the right to a fair trial. in 2008, the eu played a key role in the maldives' democratic transition process, when it pushed hard for democratic elections to end 30 years of dictatorship. but while the international community's attention was elsewhere, in 2012, the first democratically elected president nasheed resigned in unclear circumstances. the current president and the current government have not continued the process of democratization, but have unfortunately turned to some autocratic tendencies, and seem to have approached islamic extremist groups. the eu must therefore once again demonstrate its determination to support the democratisation of the country, and i hereby call on the high representative and the foreign service to use all available diplomatic tools to achieve this goal.
madam president, europe has done a lot for the maldives in many different ways, in economic terms, in cultural terms, but above all in political terms. when we talk about what we know, that the new constitution of 2008 opened a new page in the history of this island country, we are also talking about what europe has done for this country. politically, democracy was adopted, but it proved to be relatively short-lived. so i'm not here to talk about whether the current leadership is more sympathetic to china or more sympathetic to islam or more sympathetic to i don't know who, but i'm here to talk about first of all that the former president has the right to a fair trial, has the right to have a lawyer, has the right to have a doctor and to ensure that such a person who led the maldives, who led the democratic process, in cooperation and with us, it should be said openly, has the right to the protection of all his human rights.

albania in the fight against organised crime, with an intensification of law enforcement activities, and towards the reform of its judiciary. however, along much the same lines as parliament, the council also noted that important challenges still lie ahead. the council remains committed to the principle that the opening of accession negotiations would be considered by the european council, in line with established practice, once the commission had assessed that albania has achieved the necessary degree of compliance with the membership criteria. in order to open accession negotiations, albania would now need to do its part. let me remind you of five areas where albania is invited to intensify its reform efforts and to act decisively to address these key priorities. we underline in particular the need for albania: first, to continue the reform of public administration with a view to enhancing its professional capacity and impartiality; second, to pursue a comprehensive reform of its judiciary to reinforce its independence and efficiency through an inclusive process and in close consultation with the venice commission; third, to develop a coherent policy in the fight against corruption; fourth, to continue its efforts in the fight against organised crime, including against drug cultivation and trafficking; fifth, to take effective legislative and policy measures to reinforce the protection of human rights and anti-discrimination policies, including the equal treatment of all minorities, as well as to implement property rights. finally, albania needs to urgently address the identified shortcomings concerning freedom of expression and the media, and particularly to strengthen the independence of the media regulatory authority and the public service broadcaster. the council also expects the albanian authorities to ensure sustained implementation of the reforms already undertaken. i have now listed five key messages that the eu awaits from the albanian authorities. allow me now to mention additional essential elements where more work needs to be done: political dialogue, economic reforms and regional cooperation. as regards political dialogue, constructive and sustainable cooperation between the government and the opposition on eu-related reforms is vital. it is the shared responsibility of both government and opposition to ensure that political debate takes place primarily in parliament and to contribute to creating the conditions for its proper functioning. in this regard, we welcome the european parliament’s engagement in the re-establishment of the political dialogue in the parliament of albania. it is important that albanian citizens understand what the european union is about, but it is important also that they understand the government’s actions in bringing their country closer to the union. therefore, we urge albania to establish a national council for european integration, bringing together all stakeholders, which should further consolidate the nationwide consensus on eu integration. as regards economic reforms, albania should continue its efforts to increase competitiveness, to improve the business and investment environment, to achieve fiscal consolidation and to address high unemployment and the high level of informality in the economy. regional cooperation is an essential part of the eu integration process. good neighbourly relations will strengthen the country’s ability to deliver security and prosperity to its people. here i have to note the positive commitment by albania in developing regional cooperation by participating in numerous regional initiatives, such as the south-east europe cooperation process and the regional cooperation council, as well as by strengthening bilateral relations with countries of the western balkan region. likewise, the council is pleased with albania’s consistent alignment with the eu’s common foreign and security policy. the council is determined to continue its engagement with albania. we are looking forward to the next eu-albania stabilisation and association council scheduled for three weeks from now. it will be an opportunity to review the progress achieved and discuss the challenges that lie ahead. meeting these challenges will not be an easy task, but we have strong faith in albania’s ability to deliver. let me assure you that the eu is ready to support this reform process and support the people of albania in achieving a prosperous and secure future. in conclusion, i would like to express my gratitude for the excellent work that the european parliament rapporteur on albania, mr knut fleckenstein, has carried out. i am looking forward to interesting discussions.

president-in-office of the council.– mr president, this year we have to embrace change and develop a truly universal and ambitious post-2015 development agenda, aimed at poverty eradication and sustainable development in its three dimensions – economic, social and environmental. the discussion on mobilising all means of implementation, both financial and non-financial, for the post-2015 agenda, is currently accelerating both in the eu and globally. the third conference on financing for development to be held in addis ababa in july is a key trigger of this acceleration. the council notes the work done by parliament in this respect, notably the draft report on financing for development. we are looking forward to the adoption of the report during the may part-session to further inform our work. the eu has consistently accounted for more than half of global official development assistance (oda). the european union has made ambitious oda commitments, including collectively committing to 0.7 % of gni by 2015 and to 0.15-0.20 % of gni to the least developed countries. we are not shying away from our commitments and are determined to fulfil them, even if we have not yet been able to fully deliver due to an unexpected – and major – global financial and economic crisis. we stand ready to play our part. we fully recognise the importance of this element as a success factor for the negotiations in addis ababa and beyond. let me remind you that no other major development donor has made an explicit commitment or signalled readiness to reach the 0.7 % target or to significantly increase their aid levels. let me now turn to the preparation of the addis ababa conference. the latest oecd figures on oda for 2014 show that the eu and its member states have increased their aid substantially since the last period. at this stage the council is preparing the formal eu position for the conference in addis ababa, where examining the conditions and the timing for the eu to recommit collectively on oda is a key element. a first round of encouraging discussions was held at the informal meeting of ministers of development on 12 march 2015. the next discussion is to be held by the development council on 26 may 2015 when the council will adopt council conclusions. any recommitment on oda targets has important budgetary implications that require political buy-in across institutions, and constituencies are to be considered carefully by member states. this process needs to be closely coordinated with the economic, social and environmental constituencies. the council agrees that oda is important for the success of the addis ababa, new york and paris conferences. for the addis ababa conference we need a well-balanced package with oda as a part. oda still remains important for those most in need, and should be channelled accordingly. yet it is evident that oda is decreasing in relative importance to other potential resources for sustainable development. issues such as trade, remittances, support for domestic resource mobilisation and science, technology and innovation, to name just a few, can be much more interesting for a whole range of partner countries. to conclude, let me stress again the council’s position on shared responsibility. we will only be able to implement an ambitious post-2015 agenda if all countries take the necessary steps in terms of political action and resource mobilisation, and contribute meaningfully to achieving the agenda. i want to thank ms mcavan for her question and for giving me the opportunity to intervene. to reiterate, 2015 is a unique opportunity to arrive at a truly universal and sustainable development agenda, and we should use all avenues to communicate about the importance of the addis ababa, new york and paris events. i am looking forward to your views.
member of the commission.– mr president, let me thank the chair of the committee on development (deve), ms mcavan, for putting this question forward. it focuses on official development assistance (oda) which is a very important and catalytic aspect of the means of implementation for the post-2015 agenda. despite the difficult budgetary environment faced by eu member states, i am pleased that collective eu oda in 2014 reached eur 58 billion, which is the highest ever absolute level. the percentage of the eu’s gross national income (gni) spent as oda in 2014 was 0.42 %. this is significantly higher than that of other oecd donors whose oda averaged 0.28 % of gni. whilst this clearly falls short of our 0.7 % target, the eu collectively has consistently accounted for about half of the global oda as reported by the oecd. i think we can be proud of this achievement, especially during a period of serious budgetary constraints. as the commission communication of 5 february sets out, the commission believes that the eu should maintain its collective commitment to achieving the un target of providing 0.7 % of gni as oda and should also commit to the 0.15 % to 0.20 % oda target for least developed countries. the commission will continue to call for a recommitment of these existing targets. a series of meetings with member states are planned in order to facilitate agreement. however, it is ultimately for member states to reach consensus on the issue and to put in place national plans for meeting these targets. i was encouraged by the informal council meeting of the development ministers in march, where the willingness of member states to reach a common position and to uphold the eu’s place as world leader in development cooperation was very strong. i therefore hope that the council will be able to adopt clear and compelling conclusions on the global partnership next month – including on the eu’s recommitment to the oda targets. i believe this commitment matters. i fully agree with ms mcavan that an eu commitment to oda will be important for the european union’s development credibility as well as for the success of the international conferences in addis ababa, new york and paris this year. at the same time, we must recognise that to finance such a far-reaching global agenda, the eu’s efforts alone will not be enough. if we aspire to a truly ambitious outcome from addis ababa and new york, i believe a commitment to reach the 0.7 % target should be made by all developed countries. to ensure the diversity and volume of resources that will be needed by the new sustainable development goals (sdg), upper middle-income countries and emerging economies should also commit themselves to increasing their financial contributions to the development of the poorest countries. i would also like to note that oda remains an important element in the overall financing available for developing countries, and in particular countries most in need. at the same time, we have to envisage a more strategic and functional role for oda by using it in a catalytic manner to engage and leverage other financial and non-financial means of implementation that would suffice to cover such a broad new sdg agenda. a few days ago, i was in washington to attend the spring meetings of the international monetary fund and the world bank group. the discussions revealed a growing shared understanding that official development assistance must be increasingly used so as to crowd in other funding sources. agreement was clear that we need a comprehensive financial package, comprising aid, investments and domestic resources, especially effective taxation systems; and that the key factor for achieving the sustainable development goals is not only money, but also an enhancing framework of good policies and good governance. with these first considerations in mind i look forward to today’s discussion.

written. ‒ since the beginning of the conflict in syria and iraq, this is just one in a series of barbaric acts by the extremist group isis. more than 300 cultural, archaeological and religious sites in the conflict area have been destroyed. videos have also been released showing members of terrorist groups destroying religious and national symbols in the city of nimrud, one of the cities often called the cradle of civilization. isis' actions challenge the international community and show that they have no respect for the history of other cultures. unesco director irina bokova said that "the deliberate destruction of cultural heritage is a war crime". even more tragically, isis is using this crime to fund new attacks by selling the monument, which puts this issue in the broader context of counterterrorism. i supported the resolution on the destruction of cultural sites by the terrorist group isis, for which there is no justification. it's just another form of attack on the identity of a culture and a people. it calls on all religious and political leaders to rise up against the barbarism of the islamic state on the heritage of humanity.
written. ‒ i supported this resolution which sends a clear signal to the competent institutions to take all necessary actions to prevent the cultural genocide carried out by the group isis. recently, we have witnessed an intensification of the deliberate and targeted destruction of archaeological, religious and cultural sites in syria and iraq by extremist groups affiliated with the islamic state. the destruction of cultural heritage is unacceptable and therefore because cultural heritage is part of the identity and history of a people, it bears witness to the emergence and development of a civilization. i strongly condemn the actions of isis, which irrevocably destroyed the priceless treasures of ancient civilizations and impoverished our modern society. i call on all those responsible to take appropriate measures at political level to put an end to the illicit trade in cultural goods from the territories of syria and iraq, and to implement appropriate security measures at the external borders of the union to prevent the smuggling of cultural goods. i also call on the european commission to take concrete action to prevent isis from continuing its terrorist and vandal activities.
‒ the european union has ratified the convention on the protection and promotion of the diversity of cultural expressions, adopted on 20 october 2005, which is the first international instrument to recognise the dual economic and cultural nature of cultural goods and therefore 'should not be treated as having a purely commercial value'. i am pleased that on 1 march 2014, thanks to european union funding, unesco, together with other strategic partners, launched a three-year project entitled 'urgent protection of syrian heritage', which aims primarily at ensuring the urgent protection of syrian cultural heritage. while the illicit trafficking in cultural goods is still the third most important area of illicit trafficking after drug and arms trafficking, and this illicit trafficking is dominated by organised criminal networks, and since the current national and international mechanisms lack the appropriate equipment and support to tackle this problem, it is appalling that in addition, cultural heritage of immeasurable value is being completely destroyed. i join calls to support the unesco campaign #unite4heritage by launching an information campaign focusing on iraq and syria to raise awareness of the importance of their cultural heritage, the way that looted heritage is used to finance terrorist activities and the possible penalties for the illegal importation of cultural property from these countries or from third countries, and i support this resolution.
written. ‒ i thank the chair of the committee on culture and education for raising this important issue of the destruction of cultural sites by the terrorist group isis/daesh. the destruction and looting of museums and religious, historical, archaeological and cultural sites in syria and iraq, along with the recording and posting of material on the internet, demonstrates the deliberate "scorched earth" war strategy systematically implemented by the terrorist group isis. in addition to the psychological dimension of this war strategy aimed at destabilising the population and destroying identities, the terrorist group isis is also partly financed by the proceeds of the sale of archaeological artefacts, and it is therefore crucial to launch concrete measures to combat this kind of barbarism. i therefore support the european parliament resolution calling for a concrete strategy to combat this type of organised crime, for better cooperation between member states in the fight against the illicit trafficking of cultural property from war zones, for the strengthening of eurojust and europol units and for more effective use of existing international instruments. as a representative from croatia, i am particularly sensitive to this issue because of the homeland war in croatia from 1991 to 1995, during which the same strategy of the aggressors was implemented in terms of destroying and removing every trace of the existence of croatian culture, people and religion.
written. ‒ i supported the european parliament resolution on the destruction of cultural sites by the isis/daesh group. recently, numerous archaeological, religious and cultural sites in syria and iraq have been targeted for destruction by extremist groups linked in particular to the so-called islamic state in iraq and syria, and the deliberate destruction of cultural heritage for the purpose of 'cultural cleansing' has been strongly condemned. furthermore, it was important to call on the commission, the high representative, the eu and its member states to implement more effective security measures at the external borders of the eu in order to prevent the smuggling of cultural goods from syria and iraq into the union, given that the illicit trade in cultural goods is now the third largest area of illicit trafficking after drug and arms trafficking, and which finances the illicit activities of isis.
written. ‒ i support the motion for a resolution on the attack by isis/daesh on the bardo museum in tunis and the deliberate destruction of the mosul museum in iraq and of historical sites in syria. such actions take on a much larger scale than just cultural tragedies, they could be called cultural cleansing. the strategy and goal of terrorists is to destabilize populations and destroy their identity by destroying what belongs to the common heritage of humanity. according to the unesco convention on the protection and promotion of the diversity of cultural expressions, signed 10 years ago, this common heritage should be "protected and safeguarded for the benefit of all".

vice-president of the commission. – mr president, first of all, i would like to thank you cordially for this very fruitful debate. i got a clear message from this debate: we need change and that change is digital. time is very limited, but i will try to respond to as many questions as possible. i would like to start with marju lauristin. yes, i agree. some people will lose their jobs, but digital is creating many more jobs than it is destroying. but we have to help those people who lose their jobs to find new ones. we have to pay much more attention to the lifelong learning process. the cost of non-europe in a digital sense is huge. according to the latest analyses prepared by the european parliament, the cost of non-europe in this sense is eur 415 billion. i am afraid that if we do not act immediately, this cost of non—europe will even increase in the future. the commission is planning to make all its proposals during this year and next. we do not want to leave those proposals to the end of our mandate. there is a sense of urgency in the commission too. i would also like to ask you to speed up those processes. data protection reform, the network and information security (nis) directive, and the telecoms single market package are essential building blocks for a digital single market. a date for the end of roaming is something our people are really expecting to get from those negotiations. i would like to ask you to push for an end to roaming in the european union. i would like to state that very clearly.
