strong political leadership in all its external policies, including in international cooperation and development. we confirmed this intention in the recent global process of adoption of the new sustainable development goals. this is exactly what the commission’s services and the european external action service had in mind when putting forward the new framework for action on gender equality and women’s empowerment through eu external relations from 2016 to 2020. looking at its scope and substance, it is a more ambitious, robust and results-oriented successor to the current eu gender action plan in development, which will soon expire. its ambition is clearly seen in its thematic and geographical coverage: it will apply in all eu external policies, including trade and, where relevant, humanitarian assistance. it will apply in all our partner countries, including in fragile and emergency situations. it will focus on transformative areas for girls and women, so as to eliminate all forms of violence or discrimination, to give them equal access to natural and economic resources and to empower them socially and politically. let me stress this: the level of ambition and commitment of this new framework have not been affected by its format as a joint staff working document. it is a positive step change that will ensure that the commission’s services and the european external action service work together effectively, coherently and strategically, making sure that the fulfilment of girls’ and women’s rights are a tangible reality. we expect the member states to endorse our new approach soon through relevant council conclusions, by making a widely applicable and coordinated effort at eu level. i would like to invite the european parliament to join this collective endeavour, so we can maximise our impact and results on the ground. i am convinced that the change has to start from home: shifting the institutional culture – including through dedicated leadership in all european union institutions and member states – is key to ensuring a more effective delivery of gender-sensitive outcomes. rest assured that adequate financial and human resources and gender expertise to implement the new framework will be provided. for instance, specific support will be provided to our staff in eu delegations and headquarters, through helpdesks and targeted training. the commission’s commitment is also quantifiable: the development cooperation instrument has already earmarked around eur 100 million for measures targeting gender equality. much more is going to be spent by programmes tackling other sectors and priorities – like agriculture, energy, justice and migration – that consistently take women’s and girls’ perspectives into account. a strong monitoring and reporting structure is also being put into place to make all actors, at all levels, accountable for the results of implementation. in conclusion, let me reiterate our full commitment to the effective implementation of this new gender framework and to making the necessary changes happen. we hope to have parliament’s support, and i personally am sure that parliament will support this initiative for the commission.

written. ‒ this proposal for a directive aims to create a harmonised legal framework to create a single and integrated payment system in the european union. the measures covered by this proposal for a directive aim to standardise and enable the inter-operability of card, mobile and internet payment services; to encourage competition between different payment service providers with a view to increasing efficiency and transparency and security in retail payments; to encourage the cross-border use of innovative cards, internet and mobile payments in order to ensure a single market for retail payments; and to ensure adequate consumer protection in the field of payments, in particular in the area of new forms of payment. this proposal will reduce payment costs and allow new service providers to enter the market, while at the same time raising the level of security for consumers. that's why i supported the report of representative tajani.

written. ‒ the proposal for a directive is of particular importance as significant areas of the payments market, in particular card payments and online and mobile payments, remain fragmented across national borders and payment service providers face challenges in introducing innovative, secure and user-friendly digital payment services. the proposal, as amended by the european parliament, fills certain regulatory gaps, aiming to modernise the legislative framework for payment services in line with technological and market developments, increase consumer choice, encourage lower prices for payment services and improve online payment security. the amendments to the proposed directive further clarify the conditions and implications of excluding certain payment transactions from the scope of directive 2007/64/ec and extend the scope of services covered by the directive to account information and payment initiation services, with a view to increasing the transparency and security of such transactions. in order to prevent the arbitrary use of exclusion practices from the directive in different member states, service providers should be obliged to notify relevant activities to the competent authorities of the member states and a notification procedure should be provided for any exclusion based on compliance with a threshold. the commission has also concluded that the proposed directive would not be compatible with the internal market if it were to be applied in the same way as the directive on the internal market.

member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, let me begin by thanking the rapporteur, mr pargneaux, and all the members involved in the motion for a resolution we are debating today. the paris conference is a historic milestone in the international community's efforts to combat climate change. in his state of the union address to the european parliament, president juncker stressed that the european union will not accept any agreement. as the head of the european union's negotiations in paris, my job will be to ensure that the european union leads the negotiations and is not a passive spectator. and with this new global agreement we must begin a dynamic process that will enable us to effectively combat the risks of climate change and accelerate our global transition to a low-carbon and climate-responsible society. ladies and gentlemen, a key challenge during this year has been to ensure that the conference parties present their national contributions on mitigation and adaptation. to date, 150 parties have submitted their respective contributions covering almost 90% of global emissions. the european union was one of the first to do so with an ambitious target of reducing emissions by 40%. we have set an example for our partners and others are following, but we have also carried out extensive international awareness-raising work throughout the year, encouraging third countries to commit to global climate action. in this context, we are witnessing a fundamental transition from action by a few to action by the majority. comparing the contributions submitted to date with the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol - which runs until 2020 and covers only around 12% of global emissions - progress towards the paris summit is remarkable. today we see that there is a clear global political will at the highest level. i have just returned from the forum on adaptation and mitigation commitments which we have organized with the collaboration of morocco in rabat, with the participation of more than forty countries. i am particularly pleased that mr pargneaux has taken part in this forum, which has shown the participants the importance which this parliament attaches to the paris summit. although we have seen in this forum that the contributions so far presented are not sufficient to meet the objective of limiting global warming to below two degrees celsius, the good news is that these contributions already constitute a major step forward and put the target within reach. these contributions are more than just numbers, they are real strategies developed at the highest political level, and, furthermore, when we consider that many countries are designing and implementing these climate plans for the first time, we realize the progress we are making globally on climate action. but the main question is how we ensure that we get an ambitious agreement in paris and how we define its success. in my view, the answer to these questions boils down to three essential elements. first, establish a long-term goal. secondly, to ensure that the paris agreement includes the flexibility needed to strengthen its ambition over time. the new agreement must therefore include a review mechanism to enable us to assess progress and to reinforce the emission reduction targets on a regular basis in the light of the latest scientific data available to us. and thirdly, the agreement must include provisions to ensure transparency and accountability because these rules will be the foundation of a credible international regime. with the targets set, we have a tough job ahead of us. the last technical negotiating session in bonn begins next week. at this session we shall be discussing a draft agreement which was presented by the co-chairs of the negotiations on 5 october. the good news is that the new text is shorter and easier to understand. the less positive news is that the text is unbalanced, lacks ambition and specificity in many respects - including transparency and accountability - lacks a mechanism to dynamically increase mitigation ambition over time, and some key policy issues remain open. so, it will be a crucial negotiating session. ladies and gentlemen, in order to be effective in these negotiations, the european union must remain united and act with one voice. i am therefore pleased to note that in the draft resolution, and after the committee discussions, there is a common basis between the institutions and the member states. in this respect, i consider it extremely positive that the draft resolution recognizes the need for an ambitious, universally valid and legally binding agreement. i share your conviction that the paris agreement should promote a system of evaluation of objectives based on common and transparent standards, including provisions for monitoring, reporting and verification. and i strongly support the paris agreement project being sustainable and dynamic. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. climate finance will be a key issue on which the european union, moreover, and the member states have an excellent track record. significant resources from the multiannual financial framework will be allocated to climate change-related projects abroad. we expect the financial contributions to more than double to eur 2 billion a year. and as for progress towards the global $100 billion target, i'm pleased to note that the most recent estimates show that climate finance reached $62 billion in 2014, as indicated in the recent oecd report. ladies and gentlemen, let me end by stressing how important the support of the european parliament is to the negotiating position of the european union. the agreement, which is legally binding, must be ratified by parliament. the outcome of the negotiations will be presented to this house for consideration and it is therefore essential that members are associated and kept informed of the progress of the negotiations. in paris i will personally report to the european parliament delegation every day and instruct the commission's negotiating team to give parliament all the assistance it needs. but beyond the negotiations, the experience of the past few months shows how important it is for the european union to remain the global leader in the fight against climate change. and that is why we need credible and effective national and european climate policies. and the role of parliament in this respect has been very valuable. i would like to thank you, once again, for your support and enthusiasm in consolidating climate policy in the european union and in our global leadership on this matter.

written. ‒ i support the draft directive as it seeks to establish clearer, more modern and more effective guidelines for the protection of travellers and for the provision of information to potential customers of package travel arrangements. the most important provisions are the possibility of protection for travellers against the organiser's insolvency in the event of unforeseen circumstances, covering all reasonable foreseeable costs and payments of the traveller in relation to the package, and the enhanced rights of travellers and the enhanced liability of the organiser in cases of improper performance of the contract, sudden price changes and the need for compensation in the event of material and non-material damage. in the event of improper performance of the contract, the burden of proof shall be on the tour operator, as well as the obligation to find a suitable alternative arrangement for the traveller, or to provide compensation within two weeks in the event that such an alternative arrangement is not available. the proposal for a directive also provides for a clearer definition of the pre-contractual information and information on the rights of termination to be provided to customers. the adoption of such a directive would enable our citizens to enjoy their rights in the single internal market of the european union with less stress and care, to move freely and to spend their days off worthily travelling and discovering new countries and cultures.

member of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, thank you, it is a pleasure for me to be here tonight. i would also like to thank the rapporteur, mr ruas, mr blanco lópez and mr jakovčić, for the three important reports we are discussing today. i also thank mr omarjee for his comments on simplification. as you know, this commission was appointed with a clear mandate to work towards a new start for europe, based on ten major political priorities, and of course the european structural and investment funds are actively contributing to many of these priorities, as reflected in the three reports we are discussing today: the europe 2020 review, good economic governance and the current state of play of the eu strategy for the adriatic and ionian region. let me start by talking briefly about these reports, and then i'll talk about the simplification process that we're currently going through. firstly, mr ruas' report, the eu 2020 strategy; the strategy addresses five specific objectives in the following areas: employment, innovation, climate change and energy sustainability, education, and the fight against poverty and social exclusion. unfortunately, the consequences of the economic crisis, such as rising unemployment and a very slow economic recovery, have been a real obstacle to the achievement of these objectives. in this context, the commission has started a process of reflection on the future of this strategy. last year we launched a public consultation which showed that the europe 2020 strategy and its objectives are still very relevant, but that we still have a long way to go to achieve our proposed goals. i would like to welcome the suggestions of mr ruas, the rapporteur, on improving the knowledge and the need for local and regional authorities, member states and all stakeholders to take responsibility for the 2020 strategy, and i would certainly urge you to continue to mobilise national parliaments in this regard. with regard to the report by mr blanco lópez on sound economic governance, i would like to reaffirm the european commission's full commitment to act strictly within the framework provided for in article 23 of the regulation on the common provisions for these funds. these provisions were established with the aim of increasing the efficiency of european funds and, in this context, the partnership agreements and operational programmes have already been designed in accordance with the country-specific recommendations. the european commission will therefore only use its rescheduling powers where this can have a real impact on the implementation of the country-specific recommendations. in the same vein, i would like to remind you that last week the commission's communication on the next steps towards completing europe's economic and monetary union was adopted. as i have said before in this chamber, if one of the conditions for a possible suspension of the structural and investment funds is this is the third macro-regional strategy of the european union. almost exactly a year ago i was present in milan for the launch of this strategy. she was adopted last year. it aims to promote sustainable economic and social prosperity in the region and to contribute to the integration of the western balkan countries into the european union, and i welcome your report, mr jakovčić, which includes several valuable recommendations set out in detail. i would like to take this opportunity to remind you that we, the european commission, are ready to help implement the strategy, but to ensure its success, a few conditions are necessary. first, the participating countries should take responsibility and firm commitment in support of this strategy by allocating sufficient resources, administrative resources. secondly, national and regional policies, investment plans and funds allocated must be in line with the objectives of the strategy and thirdly, civil society must be effectively involved in the process of implementing the strategy, as well as national and regional parliaments. you also raised the possibility that these macro-regions could contribute more to addressing and mitigating the refugee crisis. i want to tell you that i really think we can exploit more the extent to which these macro-regions can contribute to this issue. i would just like to inform you in connection with this that together with the auditors, we have made a list of possibilities from the regional development funds, what kind of projects can be made from the regional development funds for the accommodation of refugees, for mobile hospitals, sanitation facilities, for bringing water, in the medium and long term, and i want to reassure you that we are considering any proposal coming from the member states, but it is indeed the obligation of the member states to send us to what extent they think it is necessary to change the financial allocations for this omarjee, who raised this issue, that it is a common concern of us, the european parliament and the european commission, and we want, as you do, to ensure the effective and efficient management of european funds. simplifying the funds is one of the commission's objectives for better regulation and a results-oriented budget of the european union. the high level group on simplification was set up, as you said, precisely for this purpose, and has started to work and make recommendations for concrete actions that can maximise the potential for simplification in the current programming period. as you mentioned in your question for oral answer, i can confirm that the high level group will be looking at e-cohesion, access to finance for smes, which i think is a very important topic, cost member of the commission.– mr president, this has been a really incredible debate which shows me how important the topic is. in spite of the big challenges, i know that we are going to address it in the best possible way, with all stakeholders included. let me quickly reflect on some of the members’ questions and comments. unfortunately i will not be able to reply to all of them because of the limited time available. i could speak really fast, but then our interpreters would have a real challenge, so i will try to address as many as i can. please send us additional questions if i am not able to respond to everyone. first, the issue raised most frequently was that of the safeguards on fair competition. the commission supports the objective of ensuring fair competition in the aviation sector and we have different tools in order to do this: first, by promoting sound principles of competition enforcement in the bilateral air service agreements, and second, by promoting eu-level air service agreements – especially with important trading partners – that lead to comprehensive agreements and revising the standard ‘fair competition’ clause in order to make it more usable in negotiations with third countries, while ensuring that the exclusive competence of the commission and national competition authorities in applying eu competition rules is fully respected. that will be stated very clearly. the next question related to subsidies. let me underline that the existence of subsidies is alleged and not yet proven. even if subsidies exist, we would need to see whether they have a negative impact on eu companies. that is what we are really after. let us not forget that the loss of competitiveness in the eu aviation industry is due to a number of reasons, from the continued fragmentation of the european air traffic systems and lack of implementation of the single european sky to insufficient infrastructure, and also the lack of a level playing field. the commission intends to address this in the aviation strategy. the next questions were related to regulation 868/2004. so far – which is really interesting – no complaint has been lodged by the eu in the industry under the regulation, despite frequent claims and concerns about unfair practice from third countries. the commission is therefore in the process of finalising the internal revision of regulation 868/2004. a legislative proposal as a follow-up initiative for the aviation strategy could then be expected by early 2016. regarding working conditions, in a competitive air transport market, pressure to reduce operational costs is high, which can have an impact on social matters. the commission, through the aviation strategy, aims to tackle all these challenges. eu aviation players across the entire value chain should be able to benefit fully from the growth potential to allow the maintenance of a strong social agenda and the creation of high—quality jobs. in this context, the most important thing is a very strong social dialogue. i think we established really good conditions for that at the conference on social issues in transport in june 2015. atypical forms of employment was the next most frequently mentioned challenge. it is important to have all the factual and legal elements of the developments on the market to understand the implications of the use of atypical forms of employment in aviation and the implications for the eu aviation policy. to this end, the commission will publish shortly a study on employment and working conditions in air transport and airports. furthermore, the european aviation safety agency (easa) has set up a working group to assess the safety aspects of new business models. training and skills and safety and security in europe meet the highest standards, and they must continue to do so. some skills and competences are not yet widely available and will have to be developed. training should be given a high priority. on this matter, the easa virtual academy is developing into a true european network of accredited aviation training institutions and institutes. common standards regarding the competences of aviation safety inspectors is also a matter we are looking into. the environment: the eu has also put in place powerful regulatory tools, such as the emissions trading scheme, addressing co2 emissions in the eu. a global market—based mechanism should be pursued to achieve carbon-neutral growth from 2020, as well as the option of the first ever co2 standards for aircraft. the challenges of gibraltar were also mentioned, and i would really like to address them. the gibraltar issue risks jeopardising several years’ work of three institutions, while preventing the eu from upholding its commitments in this field. we therefore continue to urge both parties to take a constructive approach and find a pragmatic solution. the aviation strategy should provide the political momentum to make progress in this field, in particular for passenger rights and ses 2+, which many members mentioned. finally, the commission intends to put forward its aviation strategy in early december. this will not be a one—off exercise – there is no magic wand – but it the beginning of a process that should lead us to a strong and competitive aviation sector and an ever-stronger single aviation market. i really look forward to continuing this close cooperation with parliament. i am hopeful that we will achieve a really important breakthrough and that european aviation will continue to be the leader on the written. ‒ for the sake of the credibility and transparency of union law, i consider it necessary to remove from the legislation in force acts which no longer serve a purpose. in addition to new acts whose entry into force makes it necessary to repeal old ones, they have also established new organisations which are functioning and have taken over tasks which would fall within the competence of the member states and other organisations and bodies. the repeal of a number of obsolete union acts from the schengen acquis at union level provides legal certainty and clarity that cannot be sufficiently achieved at member state level. in the light of the above, i consider it justified to repeal all 11 proposed decisions and council regulation (ec) no 189/2008.

written. ‒ i supported the regulation repealing certain acts of the schengen acquis, which i consider necessary in order to repeal obsolete acts which have passed the transitional period provided for by the treaty on the functioning of the european union or have been replaced by new acts. i consider that the repeal of those acts is particularly useful in order to avoid overlapping legal provisions in european union legislation. in order to simplify legislation, this regulation repeals the decisions on: visa policy, exchange of statistical data, issuing of schengen visas, evidence under readmission agreements, working group, difficulties in obtaining passports, stamping, combating illegal immigration, document advisers and liaison officers, as well as the council regulation on sis ii tests. i consider that the european commission's proposals meet the objectives of the refit programme, which aims to ensure the coherence and effectiveness of the rules, and i therefore supported this regulation.

written. ‒ the eu's position within the united nations is certainly important for the achievement of the eu's foreign policy objectives. the two international bodies share the same fundamental principles and common values that should underpin the work of each of these institutions, as well as their joint work. first of all, it should be noted that these are institutions sui generis and that the complexity of their institutional structure characterises their relationship and the possibility of cooperation. the european union has a special observer status at the un, the right to participate in the discussions, to submit proposals and amendments. the aim is to achieve greater cohesion and a genuine common foreign and security policy, so that the union's role in foreign policy becomes more prominent. it is important to note that the eu member states collectively contribute the most to the un budget, both financially and by making available human capital and technical expertise, thus achieving the 'one leader, one budget, one programme' initiative. a strong and stable eu-un partnership is essential for the un's work under all three pillars (peace and security, human rights and sustainable development) and for the eu's role as an active global actor.

written. ‒ the future of the european union is closely linked to global peace, security, development and human rights. however, the challenges facing the european union require global solutions and greater support from international partners. the eu's relationship with the un is currently not at an enviable level, although the union and its member states make the largest financial contributions to the un's general budget, peacekeeping operations, and the provision of humanitarian and development assistance. in addition, the european union, as the world's largest trading bloc, plays a major role in bilateral and multilateral trade agreements and un conventions, as the only non-state participant. for this reason, the european union needs a special status within the un. it is important to bear in mind that the un system is the world's main forum for improving global governance and represents the best forum for promoting the values and interests of the european union. i fully support the council's position, as i believe that better cooperation between the european union and the un would contribute to the achievement of the union's foreign policy objectives, in particular with regard to peace and security, terrorism, organised crime, regional conflicts, state failures.
written. ‒ the rapporteur focuses on the idea of reforming the structure of the united nations in such a way as to formalise a dual governance structure - on the one hand, the security council and on the other, the sustainable development council, which would coordinate all areas of action of the united nations, except security. although the proposal is disproportionate to the theme of the report (which does not aim at reforms within the un system itself), the fact is that the european union and its member states make the largest financial contributions to the un's general budget. in the light of the recent terrorist attacks and the security threats europe is facing on a daily basis, the union needs the support of its international partners more than ever; i therefore consider the rapporteur's call for the european union and its member states to increase their political influence within the structures of this organisation to be justified, as this process would also allow for a better implementation of international obligations. i also support the rapporteur's call for simplification of structures, budgets and working methods within the united nations, in particular with regard to the reform of the dysfunctional and often criticised economic and social council; towards economic, social, environmental and developmental efficiency. that's why i voted yes.

mr. president, the fight against tax evasion is a noble cause because allowing such a practice would be unfair and discriminatory against those who operate conscientiously and in accordance with laws and regulations. but i cannot support a report that, under the cover of this struggle, promotes a repressive tax system and the introduction of a common consolidated tax base for the whole of the european union. such initiatives seem to punish those member states which, by introducing a tax incentive policy, have become more competitive and thus shifted a share of revenue to those who have stifled entrepreneurship. i believe that such practices should not be punished but rewarded and thus encourage all member states to become more competitive and attractive for investors and entrepreneurs by reducing tax and administrative barriers. we're not going to reduce tax evasion by further stifling entrepreneurs, by increasing the power of tax administrations, or by punishing tax advisors, corporations, but solely by a more reasonable and stimulating tax policy.

member of the commission.– mr president, thank you all very much for your interventions. firstly, i want to say very strongly that we need strong european industry. we need a strong european steel industry. we need strong, modernised and innovative european industry, and this is the basis for all of our actions. of course, the steel sector that we are talking about today is a really broad economic issue. it has to be tackled both on the national and the european level. you are right that price differences are really extreme in the member states. however, member states have to deal with energy taxation, and what some of you were mentioning is true. industry needs stable energy prices, and we are working on this not only in the energy market union strategy but also in all of the documents and actions that i am taking. i also agree that we need a massive effort to support the modernisation of european industry. everything shows that we really must not – and it would be stupid if we did – become dependent on steel from outside of the eu. we need a much stronger anti-dumping policy, but i also have to mention that we are today using trade defence instruments – for example, steel anti—dumping and anti-subsidy measures, registration of imports, threat of industry – but we have to be very much stronger and very much focused on this. i am quite sure that if the steel industry – or any other industry – disappears from europe, then research, development and innovation expenditure will follow, and then the services will follow. so we have to do all that we can, together with the member states, to keep them in europe. as regards giving china free market status, i know that the issue is very sensitive and that we have to be very careful about it. this topic is now under legal analysis. the debate in the college has not started yet. i repeat: i will be very careful about it. i am fully aware that it will have a major negative impact on industry in all sectors, so we will have to carefully balance, in the college, geopolitical considerations with our industrial interest. we are currently implementing a lot of measures from the steel action plan. we will keep you updated on this, but we are also analysing the state of implementation in the context of the high level group. the next meeting of the high level group on energy-intensive industries is foreseen for 18 december – in a few weeks’ time – and it will be an occasion to discuss the issues raised today during the debate and by mr martin’s report on the base metals industry, as well as the use of the trade defence instruments. we really have to study very carefully the proposals included in the report, and we will do so. i also want to mention our finishing work on the circular economy package. i am responsible for this, together with commissioner vella. adoption by the college is foreseen for 2 december. one of the actions will concentrate on secondary raw materials. i think it is important to let you know that we also have a lot of things related to the steel industry in this package. we have to make more use of our secondary raw materials, and we have to make full use of recycled metal. this, i hope, will help our industry to produce at lower cost. in line with the conclusions of the extraordinary competitiveness council on steel of 9 november, i will convene a special high-level stakeholder conference. we should address at this conference, with all of the stakeholders, the very critical issues such as investment – including the role which the investment plan will play in these sectors – energy, the circular economy package, trade and, last but not least, research and development, in order to secure the future of our industry. i am very eager to use all possible tools that we have. i will try to coordinate the use of them. of course, not all of them are my responsibility, but i will try to coordinate all of the measures that can be taken for the future of the european steel industry.
member of the commission.– mr president, i welcome parliament’s clear and constructive feedback on the eu strategic framework on health and safety at work 2014-2020. in particular, i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr christensen, for putting forward such a rich and balanced report. this will definitely contribute to the successful implementation of the eu occupational safety and health (osh) strategic framework. the commission shares parliament’s views on the importance of strengthening risk prevention policies and promoting a culture of prevention in all companies across europe, irrespective of their size or area of activity. this is indeed about fundamental rights as well as competitiveness. in the commission work programme for 2016, adopted on 27 october, we committed to reviewing the existing occupational health and safety legislation based on a detailed ex-post evaluation. our ambition is to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the european legislative framework for protecting workers while making the rules simpler and reducing regulatory burden and red tape, in particular for small and micro-enterprises. in addition, we need to enhance the protection of workers’ health and safety and reflect recent scientific advances. i share your sense of urgency on the fight against work-related cancer. we cannot stand by whilst hundreds of thousands of people per year die from work-related cancers. there are substances for which a decade ago we did not know yet that they cause cancers, but now, with what we do know, we need to act and to protect workers from being exposed to excessive doses at work. mid-next year i intend to table a legislative proposal to extend the list of substances for which there are occupational exposure limits in place. european union policy in this area, of course, goes beyond tabling new legislative initiatives. the report draws attention to a number of issues and formulates a number of recommendations on which i would like to comment in particular. first, i do share parliament’s view on the importance of improving the implementation record of european and national occupational health and safety legislation, as only effective results on the ground can make a real difference for people in their daily working life. the report highlights the role of the ec senior labour inspectors committee as a platform for the exchange of information and collaboration between member states and the importance of sufficient resources for labour inspectorates, but effective implementation and workplace compliance with osh regulation and legislation is not only a responsibility of enforcement bodies. it is in the first place a common responsibility of employers and employees, and social partners too have an important role to play in the design and implementation of preventive measures. the tripartite european occupational safety and health agency is in bilbao and is doing excellent work in promoting health and safety campaigns and supporting implementation through user-friendly tools, in particular for smes. i welcome parliament’s support for this work. secondly, i endorse the impetus that the report gives for more awareness of gender issues in health and safety, in line with the ilo decent work agenda. the european strategic framework acknowledges that specific risks affecting women deserve particular attention and require targeted action. in this area also, the bilbao agency promotes the identification and exchange of good practice on ways to improve osh conditions for women. thirdly, i share your concerns about psychosocial risks in the workplace, including stress and depression. report after report points to stress and depression as a growing cause of absenteeism and of what one has started to call ‘presentism’, a physical presence at work but sub-optimal output because of stress-related factors. the human and economic costs are enormous. one of the priority actions foreseen in the european osh strategic framework is the identification and dissemination of good practice on preventing mental health problems. the commission has recently published a new study on mental health in the workplace which provides practical guidance for workers and employers on how to deal with this issue. the european agency for safety and health at work is active in this area, for example, with its pan-european awareness campaign on stress and psychosocial risks carried out in 2014 and 2015. the emergence of new risks does not mean that we should not continue to pay attention also to traditional health risks, such as the prevention of work-related muscular-skeletal disorders. we will pay particular attention to this in the context of our ongoing ex-post evaluation of the european legislative acquis and possible subsequent initiatives. as i have underlined before, my aim is to provide maximum protection on the ground in the most sensitive and sensible way. last but not least, i would like to thank parliament for its efforts to conclude the trilogues on the platform for the fight against undeclared work. i welcome the agreement found by the co-legislators and i do hope that the platform can start its work as soon as possible next year. as parliament’s report on health and safety recalls, undeclared work unfortunately often brings with it also precarious health and safety conditions. fighting undeclared work will thus also help us tackle some of the most dangerous and unhealthy working conditions. let me assure you once again of the commission’s commitment to high health and safety standards for workers in the european union and to modernising and simplifying the rules with a view to adapting them to new developments and better implementation on the ground. i really do appreciate your support in this endeavour.

president of the council. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, with just a few days to go until the official closing ceremony of the european year for development in luxembourg on 9 december, i am particularly pleased to have this exchange with you on this example of excellent collaboration with the european institutions, involving member states, civil society, the private sector and all those concerned with development issues. from the outset, the council and the member states of the european union have been very directly involved in the european year for development. first, in the context of the preparatory work for the adoption of the decision of the european parliament and the council, which launched the european year for development, on the basis of a commission proposal. we were thus ready, as of 1 january 2015, to celebrate and live this year under the motto "our world, our dignity, our future". together we have put in place an exceptional programme of activities to highlight the achievements of the european union, acting with the member states, as a global player and the world's leading provider of official development assistance. highlights included the inaugural session in riga and the debate in brussels on the post-2015 development agenda, with young people in particular, in the presence of un secretary-general ban ki-moon. many member states also held an official inauguration of the european year for development in their own countries, in the presence of the highest authorities, thus demonstrating their commitment to development cooperation and attracting the attention of the national media. but above all, the member states have played a key role in implementing the european year for development by bringing activities as close as another, share a sense of responsibility and solidarity. we naturally also included the private sector, because its role is paramount and development is a responsibility that we all share. we have been able to use social media and digital media to reach one of the main target groups, namely young people. young people are at the heart of the new 2030 sustainable development goals. many young people are actively involved, but it was essential to continue to support them, to inform them in their process and to arouse the interest of those who feel even less involved. 2015 was an iconic year, rich in international events directly linked to sustainable development: the milan world expo, the united nations general assembly during which the 2030 sustainable development goals were adopted , the conference on financing for development in addis ababa, the climate change conference currently taking place in paris , to name just a few of the most important. these events served as a citizens of the union, and to improve understanding of the concept of policy coherence for development. despite the difficult times we are living through, european citizens tell us that they are broadly in favour of development cooperation and that they remain in solidarity with our less favoured partners. we must do everything we can to keep this spirit alive and to continue to translate this desire for solidarity into concrete action. i should like to begin by thanking the european parliament and, in particular, mrs mcavan and her colleagues in the committee on development for their contribution to the success of this european year. next week you will be with us in luxembourg to close this year. i would also like to congratulate the spirit of interinstitutional cooperation which has enabled a joint declaration by parliament, the commission and the council to be launched within a very tight timetable, which represents the legacy of the european year for development. the declaration will be signed in luxembourg on 9 december to continue the spirit of the year and to encourage the european institutions and the member states to continue their efforts to raise awareness among european citizens beyond 31 december 2015.

written. ‒ the initiative to tackle the various tax reporting manipulations by multinational companies, all for the purpose of gaining illegal added profit, has come in handy in times of crisis when countries are facing a drop in tax revenues due to reduced economic activity. i welcome the proposal to put an end to large multinational corporations which use the lax laws of individual eu countries, and especially third countries, to make a profit, avoid paying taxes or pay less than they are supposed to. the operations of multinational corporations must have a positive effect on both the local economy and the economy of the whole country and, consequently, on its revenue side of the budget. the introduction of detailed reports on company operations and the tax system is a step forward in ensuring that companies operate in accordance with the law, but also that the beneficial impact on local economies is indeed felt. i support the introduction of a regulatory body that would consolidate all national information findings on legislative solutions, corporate profits and specific agreements between national governments and companies. the commission should also be able to take into account the impact of the tax avoidance regime on the taxpayer's tax liability.
written. ‒ i support this proposal for a decision because i believe that the establishment of a committee at eu level to deal with tax-related issues will contribute to the efficiency of tax policies and help member states in the control of tax decisions and measures. the commission shall be assisted by the special committee on taxation and the committee on budgetary control. the commission has also analysed and assessed the commission's practice of carrying out a continuous monitoring, in accordance with article 108 tfeu, of all aid schemes existing in the member states, of proposing to the member states appropriate measures necessary for the progressive development or functioning of the internal market, of verifying whether aid granted by a state or through state resources is compatible with the internal market and of ensuring that it is not used in a manner contrary to the rules. i also believe that the commission should clarify and communicate the role of the committee in order to avoid misunderstandings between member states about its role. i also believe that this committee will contribute to further integration and market opening within the european union.
written. ‒ i oppose the extension of the mandate of the taxe special committee, i.e. the establishment of the taxe ii committee for a period of six months, proposed by the epp, s&d and alde groups, arguing that the same is necessary to guarantee the successful completion of the mandate of the first taxe committee. the main arguments were that the first committee had not yet received all the necessary documentation and information requested by the commission and the member states to enable it to complete its mandate in an efficient and effective manner. the primary function of the new committee would, as indicated, be to concentrate on absorbing the information they lack and, in general, to continue to implement the recommendations made by the first committee. i consider the creation of a new taxe ii committee to be completely unnecessary and pointless for the reason that it will not provide any added value but will only have the purely formal function of completing the work of its predecessor, which is sufficiently efficient, if not more efficient, and in any case cheaper for taxpayers, and this can also be solved through the already existing forums of the european parliament, such as the econ committee's working group on taxation. that's why i voted against it.

‒ negotiations on a visa waiver agreement with dominica and four other caribbean countries started on 12 november 2014 in brussels. the agreement between the european union and the community of dominica on the short-stay visa waiver allows citizens of the european union and citizens of dominica to stay without a visa in the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver covers all categories of persons (ordinary, diplomatic, official and special passport holders) whose purpose of travel does not involve the pursuit of a paid activity. the agreement takes into account the situation of member states which do not yet apply the schengen acquis in full. the visa waiver will allow dominican citizens to stay for 90 days in any 180-day period in the territory of each of those member states (bulgaria, croatia, cyprus and romania), irrespective of the period calculated for the whole schengen area. i support the council's decision to lift the visa requirement with dominica, as i believe that by lifting the visa requirement we develop friendly relations between the contracting parties and facilitate travel by ensuring visa-free entry and short-stay for our citizens.

written. ‒ i support this amendment to the agreement between the european union and timor-leste, taking into account the recommendation of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs. the commission has also proposed to amend the agreement in order to improve relations between the countries concerned. the abolition of short-stay visas allows citizens to gain new experiences and facilitates the development of mobility. citizens who leave the eu can bring their newfound experience back to their home country, thereby further improving relations between the eu and the country in question, as well as the situation in their own country. and they indirectly promote the european union in their own country.
written. regulation (eu) no 509/2014 of the european parliament and of the council amended regulation (ec) no 539/2001 by listing third countries, including timor-leste, whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement. the agreement on the abolition of visas with timor-leste was initialled on 15 december 2014. for the union, the legal basis of the agreement is article 77 (2) (a) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), in conjunction with article 218 thereof. the agreement allows citizens of the european union and citizens of timor-leste to stay without a visa in the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period. the agreement includes a provision according to which timor-leste may suspend or terminate the application of the agreement only in respect of all member states of the european union and the union may suspend or terminate the application of the agreement only in respect of all member states. i support the council's decision to conclude the agreement between the european union and timor-leste on the short-stay visa waiver, as the objectives set by the council in its negotiating directives have been achieved and the visa waiver agreement is acceptable to the union, and the suspension provision ensures equal treatment for all eu citizens.

written. ‒ invasive alien species are unusual species that do not naturally inhabit a particular ecosystem, but have been introduced into it by intentional or unintentional introduction, and by their settlement or spread have a negative impact on biodiversity, human health or cause economic damage in the area to which they have been introduced. the european commission, by its implementing decision, sought to amend the list of invasive alien species that may cause those adverse effects in the union. however, in my opinion and in the opinion of most of my fellow members, the way the draft list was drawn up was not implemented in a way that would guarantee that the same type of evidence is used in the member states and that the same standards are applied, as was also pointed out by well-known ngos of citizens working in the field of environmental and nature protection, and i therefore supported this resolution objecting to the commission's implementing decision. unfortunately, some land plant species and mammals, although they fulfil the criteria for inclusion in that list and although risk assessments are available indicating their danger, are not included in that list. i therefore call on the commission to submit a new proposal to include in the list of invasive alien species precisely those species which are considered to be the most harmful invasive alien species in europe.

written. ‒ i support the request of parliament to ask the commission to withdraw its implementing decision (eu) 2015/2279. the genetically modified mon-øø6ø3-6 × acs-zmøø3-2 maize expresses the cp4 protein epsps which causes tolerance to the herbicide glyphosate, and the pat protein which causes tolerance to herbicides containing glufosinate-ammonium. in this way, the use of this gm maize has an advantage over other commercial varieties if it is used in combination with a herbicide containing the active substance glufosinate-ammonia, but in combination with a herbicide containing the active substance glyphosate. glufosinate-ammonia is known for its teratogenicity and glyphosate was classified as a probable human carcinogen by the international agency for research on cancer (the world health organisation's specialised cancer agency) on 20 march 2015. the use of potentially carcinogenic or known teratogenic substances in the environment is a risk i consider unwarranted. the current system for the authorisation of genetically modified food and feed is unreliable in my view, as the announced review of this procedure has not yet been carried out. in addition, the commission considers that the rejection of the proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 has created a situation in which, until the adoption of the new proposal, the right of member states to decide on their own on the use of gm food and feed on their territory is not guaranteed, which is contrary to the principle of subsidiarity.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the main objective of the dayton agreement was to stop the bloody war, and a just peace, the building of a modern state was a secondary objective, and that is what actually happened. the war has been stopped, but the conditions for a stable and functioning state in bosnia and herzegovina have not been created. the central institutions of the state are very weak and often challenged, thus making it even more difficult for the central institutions of that state to function. the return of exiles to bosnia and herzegovina is marginal. thus, according to church data, only 4% of the pre-war croats live on the territory of republika srpska. the number of bosniaks in the territory of republika srpska is somewhat more favourable, but far from satisfactory. a similar situation, not as severe as in republika srpska, is with the return of exiles to the entire territory of bosnia and herzegovina. i welcome the new approach of the european union which should enable bosnia and herzegovina to become a member of this elite society. i also welcome the reform plan adopted in bosnia and herzegovina with the assistance of the european union and look forward to the implementation, the proper implementation and the implementation of these reforms. it is certain that reforms of public administration, economic reforms and reforms of other sectors of public life will help bosnia and herzegovina to become a better state, but for real stability and unity of this asymmetrically designed state, constitutional changes are needed, namely changes to the dayton constitution and this on the principles of federalism, decentralization and subsidiarity.
mr. president, it's been 20 years since the signing of the agreement that ended the war in bosnia and herzegovina. dayton was a temporary solution that was supposed to stop the bloodshed, and then in peaceful conditions to experience an upgrade that would allow bosnia and herzegovina to develop into a normally ordered state. many today still call for such an upgrade, unaware that it has already occurred on several occasions. namely, with more than 300 directives that have never been ratified by any body of the state of bosnia and herzegovina, various high representatives have significantly changed what was signed in dayton without the possibility of appeal by citizens and their legitimate representatives. so if we are to revise or significantly upgrade the dayton peace agreement, we must first of all revise the role of the high representative, who, without any democratic legitimacy, adopts directives that have greater force than the original agreement. i hope that in a joint resolution we will adopt my wording in which i ask that any future restructuring of bosnia and herzegovina guarantee true equality to all three constituent peoples. this means that the high representative will no longer have a place in that country, at least not with the powers he has so far, because it is he who has most often and without any consequences violated the principle of equality by unilateral decisions and disturbed the difficult-to-achieve political balance between the representatives of the three nations.
mr. president, 20 years after the signing of the dayton agreement, we can say that its achievement is the peaceful coexistence of the citizens of bosnia and herzegovina. the eu and its member states will continue to work together to ensure that the eu and its member states are able to implement the relevant international instruments and instruments, including the unfccc, in a way that is consistent with the principles of the charter of the united nations. but today in bosnia and herzegovina we must look for solutions to social and economic problems. during my recent visit to sarajevo as part of the delegation of the green/european free alliance club, on the occasion of the anniversary of the signing of the general peace agreement in bosnia and herzegovina, i met with young people, regardless of their nationality, who pointed out to me the social problems their peers face on a daily basis due to the unpromising political situation in the country. we are all aware of the burden of the past that overshadows the burning problems of the present. the political system, burdened with itself, so complicated that neither the citizens of bosnia and herzegovina understand it, and probably not even its politicians, leaves no much needed space for the fight against unemployment and poverty. every day bosnia and herzegovina loses its young people who leave the country in search of a secure future that they cannot find in their own country. bosnia and herzegovina is experiencing a demographic collapse. the european union must therefore call on the political elite of bosnia and herzegovina to take responsibility and reform the political system so that bosnia and herzegovina can finally embark on the path towards eu membership.

mr. president, farmers throughout history, and even today, are the world's first seed growers. their role is important for food security, biodiversity, adaptation to climate change and therefore farmers must retain the right to grow their own seeds, adapted to local conditions. plant varieties are normally protected by plant variety rights, which is a better form of intellectual property because it allows farmers to use protected varieties to create new ones. patents, on the other hand, block the flow of genetic resources, hinder research and lead to monopolies. european legislation does not allow the patenting of animal and plant varieties and of biological processes necessary for the production of plants and animals. i am strongly opposed to the patenting of life and am outraged by the decision of the european patent office which ruled in the case of 'tomatoes and broccoli' that plant products derived from conventional farming can be protected as patents. i consider such a decision illegal and unethical and i expect the european commission to react immediately. i'm betting that farmers will be allowed to grow their own seeds without interference because they've been the guardians of it for thousands of years.

written. ‒ december of this year marks the 20th anniversary of the signing of the framework agreement for peace in bosnia and herzegovina and the dayton peace agreement. the aim of the treaty was to stop the war and ensure the equality of the three constituent peoples. with the frequent amendments that have been made over the last 20 years, the original dayton agreement has been denied in a way and has ceased to exist, because with the amendments, the equality of the three constituent peoples has ceased to exist. the commission has also provided a number of recommendations to the council and the european parliament on the future of the eu. i fully support this resolution, because i think it's obvious that after a peace agreement like this, a real constitution should have followed in order for the state to function at full capacity. the country is economically very poor and has no opportunity to develop, there is a big problem of young people leaving, but also any form of corruption. the only solution is a new state restructuring, where the running of the state will be left entirely to its citizens, i.e. their legal and legitimate representatives.
written. ‒ this year, the european parliament is commemorating the 20th anniversary of the dayton peace agreement, signed in paris in december 1995. as a representative of croatia, the only eu member state directly involved in europe's bloodiest conflict since the second world war, this resolution is of particular importance to me. although the agreement ended the three-and-a-half-year war in bosnia, it was essentially a ceasefire measure that has sadly remained in effect to this day. the agreement preserved bosnia and herzegovina as a single state consisting of two parts, but in reality it has never been more divided at the national level than it is today. the dayton solution failed to turn bosnia and herzegovina into a functioning and modern european state - and as a result, the european council decided two months ago that bosnia and herzegovina would have to undergo many and comprehensive reforms before joining the european union. i myself participated in the drafting of the resolution on behalf of my group of european conservatives and reformists, in which i asked that the institutions of the european union, in the course of the accession negotiations with bosnia and herzegovina, demand genuine respect for the equality of the croatian people as one of the three constituent peoples in bih.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on arms exports: implementation of common position 2008/944/cfsp, as this issue is of great importance at a time when the eu environment is extremely volatile politically and in terms of security. weapons in the hands of irresponsible individuals become a terrorist threat. the uncontrolled proliferation of weapons poses a serious risk to peace, security, human rights and sustainable development in the world. the commission should be able to take appropriate measures to ensure that the implementation of this regulation is consistent with the objectives of the union's external action. we need more transparency and control. arms export control is an integral part of the eu's foreign and security policy and must be consistent with the principles of promoting democracy and the rule of law and preserving peace, preventing conflict and strengthening international security. i support the entry into force of the arms trade treaty. the criteria set out in the common position should be interpreted and applied by member states in a uniform manner, without economic considerations being given precedence in the decision-making. the creation of an independent european arms control body and greater attention to dual-use technologies is needed.
written. ‒ i do not support the motion for a resolution of the ep on arms exports and the implementation of common position 2008/944/cfsp. i do not think that it highlights adequately the necessary steps that member states should take in the future to put this common position into practice and to ensure that european policy remains credible in highlighting the core values of protecting human life, preventing conflict, promoting internal stability and avoiding war as a way of solving internal problems between warring parties within or between states. i hope that member states will take seriously the problem of arms exports and trade and control official and unofficial sales channels, especially smugglers. on the other hand, i hope that the problem of numerous regional conflicts in europe's neighbourhood will encourage the competent authorities within the union to approach the institutionalisation of the problem of arms transfers between the member states of the european union, but also towards third countries, more studiously. accordingly, candidate countries must be clearly required not to be platforms for manipulation of arms sales channels and be required to strictly enforce the existing legislative framework.
written. ‒ despite the eu's efforts to promote the ratification of the att and the fact that the union has a single legally binding framework for arms export controls, the level of controls is not sufficient given the data on the amount of arms ending up in the wrong hands and the fact that some eu member states are among the world's leading arms exporters and that these exports are increasing due to decreasing revenues in europe. the commission also found that the exporting producers in the prc were not able to provide the export price to the union market in the form of a price undercutting calculation. i support the call for a more thorough assessment of the risks associated with exporting countries and for a stricter adherence to the common position in order to prevent the dangerous and disruptive possibility of the union indirectly arming terrorists and repressive regimes.
written. i support the motion for a resolution of the european parliament on arms exports: implementation of common position 2008/944/cfsp, tabled by mr bodil valero. in order to ensure that the export of such weapons is not subject to arbitrary restrictions, the parties shall cooperate with each other in the implementation of the arms embargo. given that the uncontrolled proliferation of weapons poses a major danger to eu countries and the international community, and poses a serious threat to the maintenance of peace and security, i believe that the regulation of international trade should indeed be a global objective. in this context, we should particularly take into account the eu's significantly changed environment, particularly in the south and east, and the fact that third countries such as albania, bosnia and herzegovina, macedonia, iceland, canada, montenegro and norway have also formally committed themselves to the criteria and principles set out in the common position. the only legitimate export is one that strictly adheres to the criteria of common position 2008/944/cfsp and takes place in the context of the eu's response to a request concerning the right of self-defence. we must not forget that the illegal, unlawful and unregulated transfer of arms threatens political stability and hinders democratic, social and economic development.
written. ‒ i supported this report because arms export control is an integral part of the eu's foreign and security policy and should be guided by the principles enshrined in article 21 teu, in particular the principles of promoting democracy and the rule of law and preserving peace, preventing conflict and strengthening international security. i am concerned about the possible circumvention of eu export controls by licensed production in third countries or through overseas branches of companies established in the eu. i believe that there is a need for stricter control of brokering services and related activities in the arms trade at eu level, which could escape scrutiny due to the fact that these practices differ from country to country. i therefore call for the establishment and implementation of a registration system which will oblige intermediaries to report in detail on their activities.
written. ‒ the global security environment around the eu has changed dramatically, and uncontrolled proliferation of weapons poses a serious risk to peace, security, human rights and sustainable development. the eu countries have therefore signed common position 2008/944/cfsp on the maintenance of regional peace, security and stability, which sets out eight criteria for conventional arms exports that eu member states must apply when taking licensing decisions. eu member states' arms exports in 2013 totalled eur 36,7 billion, of which eur 26,7 billion (or 36% of total arms exports) were exported to third countries, and few can argue that these trade flows are of direct security interest to the eu. i accept the council's position at first reading on arms exports as i believe that a consistent interpretation and successful implementation of the measures contained in common position 2008/944/cfsp would make a crucial contribution to the achievement of the eu's objectives of development policy coherence, peace, security and human rights. however, given that the report also covers some aspects with which i do not entirely agree, i voted 'abstention'.
written. ‒ this report by the green group's own-initiative rapporteur valero seeks to push for a strict implementation of the union's common foreign and security policy in the arms export segment by eu member states to third countries. the proposal constitutes another attempt at a serious breach of the principle of subsidiarity, since it requires the european commission to be given exclusive competence at the expense of individual member states of the union. i cannot support certain calls directed at member states, such as the call for support in the creation of an independent european arms control agency under the auspices of the high commissioner for foreign affairs and security policy of the union, which would be empowered to issue an opinion to those member states which intend to issue an export licence on their territory, because i am firmly convinced that security policy has always been, and should continue to be, in the hands of individual member states of the union.
written. ‒ recent decisions by the enlarged board of appeal of the european patent office have made it possible to patent plant traits, even when they are obtained by essentially biological breeding and cross-breeding techniques. the european patent office has decided that it is competent to grant patents on plant characteristics obtained by natural crossing. someone at that institution thought he was a divine being and had copyright on nature! such a decision could have far-reaching and disastrous consequences for european agriculture, and in particular for smallholders and farmers. that is why i supported the resolution calling on the commission to examine the legal basis of the decisions of the european patent office.
written. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on patents and plant breeders' rights because i consider it necessary for the european commission to give an opinion on the interpretation of directive 98/44/ec in order to ensure legal clarity regarding the prohibition of patenting products obtained through biological processes and to clarify that patents allow the cultivation of biological material. in this context, it is necessary to encourage innovation and the development of new species in order to ensure food security, mitigate the effects of climate change and prevent monopolies within the crop sector. i also believe that we need to be particularly careful when it comes to biotechnology and genetic engineering, and i therefore support this resolution.
written. ‒ i supported the european parliament resolution calling on the commission to clarify directive 98/44/ec to ensure legal clarity on the prohibition of patenting products obtained from biological processes and defining the use of materials obtained from biological processes for plant breeding. properly defined plant regulations are essential for the development of new varieties in order to ensure global food security, combat climate change and prevent monopolies in the breeding sector. at the same time, it protects intellectual property and encourages innovation.
written. ‒ without going into the procedures and reasons followed by the enlarged board of appeal of the european patent office in reaching its decision in the 'tomatoes and broccoli' case, it is clear that european legislation refers to the fact that the patenting of animal and plant varieties and of the biological processes necessary for the production of plants and animals may not be carried out. the european parliament has already warned that legislation in this regard must be clear, as any ambiguity not only undermines the innovative potential of the plant breeding sector to develop new varieties, but also poses a threat to world food production and food security, as well as weakening the eu's position in international trade relations. i also believe that it is necessary to ensure the absolutely unrestricted use of biological material, not only for companies in the plant breeding sector, but also for farmers who use existing biological material and available techniques to produce new innovative and resistant varieties, because they have been doing so unhindered for thousands of years. i would like to remind you that european law is based on principles and that european union rules must be interpreted in their entirety, bearing in mind their true purpose and objective, since it is not always possible to foresee all the circumstances surrounding them. for all these reasons, i supported this resolution of the european parliament.
written. ‒ plant breeding is an innovative process that farmers and farming communities have been doing since the beginning of agriculture, and non-proprietary varieties and breeding methods are important for genetic diversity. access to plant-based biological material is needed to stimulate innovation and the development of new varieties to ensure global food security, tackle climate change and prevent monopolies. products obtained by processes which are essentially biological, such as plants, seeds, originating properties and genes, should therefore be excluded from patentability. the prohibition of the patentability of products obtained by processes which are biological, such as crossing, is necessary for the maintenance of innovation, food safety as well as for small farmers. i therefore join the calls for the commission and the patent office to explain their decision to parliament as soon as possible.
written. ‒ i support this proposal because it encourages innovation and economic growth. i believe it is important to enable products to obtain a european patent in order to be as competitive as possible on the market and to make the european union as visible and as visible as possible on the global market. this certification would make it easier for all eu citizens to do business and to protect their patent rights, which is one of the main objectives of investment protection. this proposal shows that the european union cares about and invests in science and innovation and that efforts in these fields should be continued.
written. ‒ access to biological plant material that captures plant properties is a key prerequisite for giving a strong impetus to growth and innovation, and for developing new varieties. the development of new varieties would ensure global food security, tackle climate change, prevent a monopoly in the breeding sector and create more opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises. products obtained by processes that are essentially biological, such as plants, seeds, original properties and genes, should not be patentable. therefore, the holder of a plant variety right cannot prohibit others from using the protected plants for further cultivation, which is a fundamental principle of the international system of plant variety rights based on the international convention for the protection of new varieties of plants (upov convention) and the eu system based on council regulation (ec) no 2100/94. i fully support the first reading of that resolution, as i believe that it is necessary to define clear rights for plant breeders and criteria for patenting. intellectual property rights are of paramount importance for maintaining economic incentives for the development of new plant products and guaranteeing competitiveness.
