written. i support the motion for a resolution on the situation in burundi tabled by mr tannock, mr demesmaeker, mr raffaele fitto and mr notis marias. given the sharp deterioration of the situation in burundi over the past few weeks and the widespread violations of human rights, and given the crucial role of respect for human rights, democratic principles and the rule of law in the eu-burundi relations governed by the cotonou agreement, the eu has a duty to defend human rights and to call for the restoration of democratic order and the rule of law. the violation of fundamental human rights, the disruption of civil institutions, the violation of media freedom have led to the displacement of more than 200 000 people. as un security council resolution 2248 strongly encourages the government of burundi to respect and protect human rights and freedoms and to agree to participate in the mediation led by the east african community, the african union, with the aim of establishing a dialogue within burundi, i consider this to be the only effective solution to the current crisis.
written. ‒ in recent weeks, the situation in burundi has deteriorated sharply, and the security forces in that country continue to violate human rights without fear of punishment. on 13 november 2015, the un special envoy for burundi stated that the situation in burundi is deteriorating and that serious human rights violations are taking place on a daily basis, including extrajudicial executions, arbitrary arrests and detentions, torture, attacks on the independence of the media, and harassment and killings of human rights defenders, as well as unjustified restrictions on the rights to peaceful assembly and expression, and that more than 200 000 people have been displaced by the violence. i am deeply concerned about the increasing human rights violations and violence in burundi, the growing divisions in society and the lack of dialogue among burundian stakeholders, and the risk of a regional crisis, and i call on all parties in burundi to stop the spiral of violence.
written. ‒ burundi has signed the peace and reconciliation agreement which stipulates that the president can only serve two terms. president pierre nkurunziza announced on 26 april 2015 that he would run for a third term in office after serving two terms. on the basis of the results of 26 august 2015, he was declared the winner, which led the country to the biggest political crisis since the end of the civil war. as the country's unrest grew, police used excessive force to suppress peaceful protests, resulting in 129 deaths. on 28 may of the same year, the eu suspended the election observation mission because the minimum conditions for holding democratic elections were not met. the international community does not consider the election valid. the political impasse in the country and the deteriorating security and economic situation have severe consequences for the population and threaten the stability of the entire region. i support the resolution on the situation in burundi because i believe that human rights must be protected, that politically motivated violence, summary and extrajudicial executions, arbitrary arrests and detentions must be punished. burundi was one of the first countries in the region, along with rwanda and congo, to hold elections and was therefore to serve as an example of respect for the international and constitutional order necessary for the sustainability of democratization, peace and development in the region.
written. ‒ this resolution builds on the statement by the high commissioner of 25 november this year. the situation in burundi has deteriorated significantly in recent weeks - security forces are increasingly brutally violating the basic human rights of burundian citizens with impunity. at least 240 people have been killed and 210,000 people have fled the country since president nkurunziza made the controversial decision to extend his presidential term. i also support the call in this resolution for a solution to the crisis to be agreed within burundi and to be based on consensus. in line with this, all political parties in burundi are called upon to end the violence and to start dialogue.

written. ‒ virunga national park is africa's oldest national park, renowned for its unique habitats and rich biodiversity, especially the endangered mountain gorillas. it is essential to prevent irreversible damage to virunga national park, which has been on the unesco world heritage list since 1979 and on the list of world heritage in danger since 1994. the damage to virunga np may result from oil exploration and exploitation and other illegal activities. fishing in lake edward provides about $30 million a year for the local community living nearby, and according to independent research by the wwf, more than 50,000 families use the lake as a source of fresh water. so i supported a resolution by representative linda mcavan calling for the protection of virunga national park.
written. ‒ i support the resolution on the protection of virunga national park in the democratic republic of congo, as according to all relevant indicators this national park is threatened by the destruction of the flora and fauna that make it special, on the basis of which it is inscribed on the unesco world heritage list and the list of world heritage in danger. i believe that the necessary steps must be taken, as this resolution clearly identifies, to secure the financial and organizational resources to ensure the smooth operation of the national park, to protect its integrity, to prevent the irresponsible and unacceptable exploitation of the natural and environmental resources, and to protect it from armed groups that threaten the survival of the park. the current activities within the protected area that pose a threat must be limited by the action of the government of the democratic republic of the congo in cooperation and with the assistance of the european union and other relevant actors at the united nations. as the national park represents an important segment of the local economy, it is necessary to do everything to ensure that the local population remains actively involved in the protection and enjoyment of the benefits of the park, but also to prevent possible environmental devastation due to the intention of oil exploitation, whose deposits cover 85% of the protected area. the protection of habitats and their associated wildlife must remain an absolute priority.

written. ‒ virunga national park, located in the democratic republic of the congo, is the oldest national park in africa. since 1978, it has been a unesco world heritage site, and it is home to many endangered species, some of which are among the last remaining on the planet. sadly, the same park has also become one of the most dangerous places in the world for wildlife conservation. the agreement with the authorities of the democratic republic of congo includes illegal oil exploration and extraction in the park, as well as a number of other illicit activities, such as poaching and ivory trade. at the same time, the park is experiencing violence linked to and instigated by armed guerrillas, and at the same time, serious violations of fundamental human rights. i support the resolution calling on the european external action service to take more decisive steps to convince the authorities in the democratic republic of congo to investigate the actions leading to violations of fundamental human rights on their territory and to take steps to stop cooperation with oil companies exploiting oil in the park, which could otherwise have cardinal negative consequences.
